#121321. GTA 6's Japanese version only partially obscures male nudity by putting Jason in a thong, seemingly due to regional censorship

GTA 6's Japanese version only partially obscures male nudity by putting Jason in a thong, seemingly due to regional censorship

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (441 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 is slowly rolling out across the globe.
  • Last week, we reported that GTA 6 might have been censored in Japan since the region's age rating board lacked any mention of the "sexual content" we knew it would include elsewhere.
  • Industry observers note that now that GTA 6 is finally in the hands of players, we have a better idea of what was left out and/or covered up in Japan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is slowly rolling out across the globe. The crime epic's already available to play in countries such as South Korea and New Zealand, but Japanese players are finding out that male nudity is only partially obscured by a thin black thong that covers Jason and the other men in Leonida.

Last week, we reported that GTA 6 might have been censored in Japan since the region's age rating board lacked any mention of the "sexual content" we knew it would include elsewhere. The Japanese version's install size was also notably smaller than other places in the world.

Industry observers note that now that GTA 6 is finally in the hands of players, we have a better idea of what was left out and/or covered up in Japan. Multiple social media accounts playing the game in Japan have reported that when you take main man Jason into the shower, his butt is only kinda covered up by a thong. At least in the version I played, Jason is usually fully naked while washing up.

GTA 6 censorship on the Japanese version is kinda funny lol https://t.co/u8v0f0cqz0.

エロシーンきた！　#GTA6 #GTAVI https://t.co/RKOEtkONlJ.

Another social media post spots a different male NPC wearing a very similar black thong during a cutscene that normally has him laid bare in international versions of the game. I'm guessing all instances of male nudity might be obscured similarly in GTA 6's Japanese version.

GTA 6 is far from the only game that's dealt with regional censorship in Japan, however. Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher 3 had their most salacious scenes censored in some manner, for example. And even GTA 5 had to remove its infamous torture scene for approval in Japan. It's quite possible GTA 6 has had to cover more than just the backside of nude men to go on sale in the country, although those regional differences won't become entirely clear until players get further through the story.

Industry observers note that ahead of the game's full launch, GTA 6 managed to break Reddit and viewership records on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. Interesting tidbits are also flying out on release day, like the fact you can't replay missions or use cheats until finishing the story. Our Chris Tapsell still had a cracking time with the epic open worlder. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," he wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

Phil Spencer Might Not Be At Xbox Anymore, But He's Still Playing Loads Of Games

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Phil Spencer is a legend of the Xbox division, having helped redefine the brand after a disastarous Xbox One launch in 2013, and spearheading such initiatives as Xbox Game Pass, Xbox backwards compatibility, crossplay, and a renewed focus on gaming rather than continuing the push towards "TV, TV, TV" that had proven so controversial.
  • It's very possible that without his influence, Xbox would have shut its doors over a decade ago.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Phil Spencer is a legend of the Xbox division, having helped redefine the brand after a disastarous Xbox One launch in 2013, and spearheading such initiatives as Xbox Game Pass, Xbox backwards compatibility, crossplay, and a renewed focus on gaming rather than continuing the push towards "TV, TV, TV" that had proven so controversial.

It's very possible that without his influence, Xbox would have shut its doors over a decade ago.

We haven't heard anything from Spencer since he announced his retirement earlier in 2026, but he's still very actively playing games on his Xbox consoles, including some of this year's upcoming releases.

For example, he's racked up 940/1000 gamerscore in Echo Generation 2, 650/1000 in Forza Horizon 6, 585/1000 in Replaced, and he's also been playing the likes of Halo: Campaign Evolved, Gears of War: E-Day, Sopa - Tale of the Stolen Potato, Baldur's Gate 3, Vampire Crawlers and even Sunset Overdrive in recent months.

One of Phil's most beloved qualities as Xbox boss was that he proved himself to be a hardcore gamer, being someone who actively seeks to play games in his spare time. Latest Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is somewhat the opposite, admitting back in February that she doesn't "pretend to be the best gamer" and that it's ultimately not her goal to be.

Anyway, Phil is busy enjoying his retirement right now, and we wish him all the best from everyone here at Pure Xbox. We unfortunately never got a chance to meet the man ourselves, but always admired his leadership from afar.

Here's hoping he might start hitting the interview circuit and doing what the likes of Peter Moore and Nintendo's Reggie Fils-Aimé have done in the past, as we'd love to see him sticking around the industry in some capacity going forward.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just under one month after legendary actor Patrick Stewart sadly passed away, Marvel boss Kevin Feige and Avengers: Doomsday directors Joe and Anthony Russo have opened up about the star's final day on set of the upcoming movie.
  • It has been revealed that "He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew," noted Feige to Entertainment Weekly.
  • Co-director Anthony Russo noted the star "muscled through" his performance even though "It was clear that he was struggling with his health." Russo added that there was an "intensely emotional" atmosphere that day and "It was in the back of all of our heads, we may never see him on set again.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just under one month after legendary actor Patrick Stewart sadly passed away, Marvel boss Kevin Feige and Avengers: Doomsday directors Joe and Anthony Russo have opened up about the star's final day on set of the upcoming movie.

It has been revealed that "He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew," noted Feige to Entertainment Weekly. "We didn’t know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was." Stewart passed away on October 28 after a brief battle with Alzheimer's and Dementia. Doomsday is Stewart final project.

Co-director Anthony Russo noted the star "muscled through" his performance even though "It was clear that he was struggling with his health." Russo added that there was an "intensely emotional" atmosphere that day and "It was in the back of all of our heads, we may never see him on set again.".

"You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others," added Anthony Russo, who is co-directing the movie alongside his brother Joe Russo. "It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that.".

Industry observers note that stewart reprises his role as mutant Charles Xavier in Doomsday, a character he has been playing for over two decades. Stewart was introduced to the world of Marvel back in 2000 in the first X-Men movie. Doomsday marks Stewart's ninth time playing the telepathic X-Men leader. Entertainment Weekly notes that Stewart was offered a role in Avengers: Secret Wars, which is set to hit cinemas next December, but he declined.

Recent findings suggest that feige has confirmed that the team is planning on including a tribute to Stewart in the fresh movie. "We’re long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us," said Feige, "We’re looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.” Avengers: Doomsday arrives in cinemas on December 16 in the UK and December 18 in the UK.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: It really seems like Xbox isn't allowed to say GTA 6 at all

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (521 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • In a recent development, as pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the significant release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles.
  • It has been revealed that "Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is notable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

In a recent development, as pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the significant release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

It has been revealed that "Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is notable. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either.".

One day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

Going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe.".

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

Now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

So what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

This is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Massive Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. In Eurogamer's five-star review, Chris Tapsell wrote, "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

OG Christmas Vacation Director Gets Real About How Feud With Chevy Chase Made Him Quit The Film

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (615 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that chris Columbus directed Home Alone, but he came remarkably close to spending Christmas with the Griswolds instead.
  • OnWildmen, the podcast hosted by Dylan Sprouse and the director's son Brendan Columbus, he revisited the feud that's been part of Hollywood lore for years.
  • I did not get along with Chevy Chase, and at this point famously now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that chris Columbus directed Home Alone, but he came remarkably close to spending Christmas with the Griswolds instead. Before that movie became a holiday staple, he was supposed to direct National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation. Then he met Chevy Chase, and Columbus' latest account makes his decision to walk away sound even gutsier than I realized.

OnWildmen, the podcast hosted by Dylan Sprouse and the director's son Brendan Columbus, he revisited the feud that's been part of Hollywood lore for years. I've heard the basic story before. What caught my attention was how badly he needed that movie, and how carefully he now talks about Chase. Columbus didn't dance around the history when the conversation turned to his early directing career:.

I did not get along with Chevy Chase, and at this point famously now.

Columbus was coming off 1988's Heartbreak Hotel, which left him convinced his directing career might be over. He'd returned to Chicago and was staying with his in-laws when John Hughes called. The Christmas Vacation offer was supposed to get him back behind the camera, and he'd already started shooting second-unit footage.

The filmmaker has spoken harshly about Chase before. But this time, he stated he's less interested in adding to the actor's bad press. Then he recalled how things reached the point where he called Hughes and quit:.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve reached a point where I disliked him so much, and had so much anger toward him, I think I’ve become mature enough, and I think he’s taken so much shit in the press for the past five years that I’m sort of like I’m tired — I don’t wanna say he’s a bad person. So, basically, because I didn’t get along with Chevy, I had to tell John Hughes. I stated, ‘I can’t do the movie.' And I needed the movie desperately. I had already shot second unit on the movie for Christmas stuff in Chicago.

I appreciate that Columbus is making room for a little perspective here. He didn't suddenly declare the feud resolved or pretend the experience was pleasant. He just sounds tired of spending another interview beating up Chase. Fair enough. I'd be tired of telling that story, too, especially knowing it started with a job he desperately needed. But the Harry Potter franchise filmmaker continued:.

Two weeks later, John sends me Home Alone. He states, ‘Okay, you can't direct Christmas Vacation. I got this other script.’.

Jeremiah S. Chechik took over Christmas Vacation, and Home Alone arrived in theaters in 1990. I'm grateful both movies became Christmas classics, although it's amusing to imagine what Columbus might have done with Clark Griswold's disastrous holiday lighting display. Given those early meetings, I suspect he'd rather not imagine it at all.

Sources indicate that hearing Columbus discuss the timing makes it even stranger. A decision that could have ended his directing career led him to Kevin McCallister, Joe Pesci, and one of the most rewatchable Christmas movies around. I think I'm going to look at the opening credits a little differently this year. Excuse me while I go rewatch Home Alone for the 100th time with my Disney+ subscription.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the original Darkest Dungeon may have gotten some latest DLC earlier this year, but that doesn't mean that Red Hook Studios are abandoning their sequel.
  • It has been revealed that it's called The Butcher's Asylum, as pleasant a name as any other, and it's a "stand alone gladiatorial arena game mode," that's due for release sometime in 2027.
  • In a recent development, this DLC isn't veering too far away from its roguelite origins, as it is still run-based, just on the shorter side and focusing more on the combat system.

According to recent reports, the original Darkest Dungeon may have gotten some latest DLC earlier this year, but that doesn't mean that Red Hook Studios are abandoning their sequel. No, in fact the next bit of DLC for Darkest Dungeon 2 was teased only a couple of weeks ago, with a new trailer shared today actually showing off what it's all about.

It has been revealed that it's called The Butcher's Asylum, as pleasant a name as any other, and it's a "stand alone gladiatorial arena game mode," that's due for release sometime in 2027. "The long-silent bells of the remote Asylum ring once more - souring the valley below with discordant and unsettling vibrations," the DLC's Steam page describes. "Garish heraldry, hastily stitched by unskilled hands, festoons the hilltop. Deep within the crumbling masonry of the Asylum, frenzied inmates compete in merciless bloodsport with monsters corralled the kingdom over. And to the victors of these debauched contests, the Butcher’s favour: a cure for their madness.".

In a recent development, this DLC isn't veering too far away from its roguelite origins, as it is still run-based, just on the shorter side and focusing more on the combat system. On your runs you'll need to prepare for the fights ahead, come across "insane enemy combinations never before possible," and spin a fun wheel which nets you prizes like newly introduced battle modifiers, charms and jinxes. There's also a new crowd meter, "a unique feature to the Asylum, can grant powerful effects to your team if you cater to the Crowd's demands. Failing to do so will only earn their scorn which raises the stakes and puts your success in jeopardy!".

It has been revealed that the Butcher's Asylum also introduces a new playable character, The Ringmaster. You pick her up by winning bouts in the arena, and then you can recruit her in any game mode. She also serves as the narrator for the DLC, likely because of the passing of the main game's narrator Wayne June; Red Hook made clear earlier this year that they would never use generative AI to recreate June's voice, so I'm glad to see they haven't backstracked here.

It has been revealed that with Grand Theft Auto 6 launching late last night (unless you're in Latest Zealand, in-person or otherwise), players have been flocking to online spaces to share their favourite moments. Lords of the Fallen 2 is officially targeting an April 2027 release date, having been hit with a lengthy delay back in the summer.

The anticipated action RPG was previously eyeing an autumn / fall 2026 launch, which would have only added to an insane PS5 schedule. Shifting to a vague 'Q1 2027' window seemed a wise move at the time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek appears to have followed through on their threat to release the executable of the Xbox build of GTA 6 they put into the wild last week, calling it "an early Christmas gift" for followers and explicitly linking the leak to efforts to recreate the game on PC: "The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects.".

Cyberleek released a near-complete build of GTA 6 late last week, holding back only the main exe—the part that makes everything else run, basically—until either their crypto coin achieved a $15 million market cap, or November 23, whichever came first. The crypto missed badly, but time marches on, and so here we are.

Industry observers note that the release of the exe, naturally, includes a call for more "donations" in its readme file (via Reddit) which Cyberleek remarked will go toward a secretive project "for the gamers." They also taunted Take-Two Interactive's efforts to track them down: "Months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving. No budget makes a lock unbreakable, and no court order deletes what the internet already has.".

Recent findings suggest that leaks in the game industry aren't anything upcoming, but this case is unique: GTA 6, effectively the biggest videogame of all time, still hasn't been revealed for PC, as is Take-Two's way. But the advent of AI means the game could be emulated on our platform far more swiftly than was possible in the past—some modders estimated it could happen within a week.

One of the leads on the Leonida recomp project predicted that things will start to move quickly from here:.

At the same time, Shayder tempered expectations in a message on the Leonida Discord, saying "it will take at least a week" for the project to reach the point where GTA will be playable on PC.

How that unofficial emulated made-with-AI build would compare to the real deal is an open question, and I strongly suspect the answer will be "not well," but even just having something GTA 6-ish playable on PC is a headache that I'm pretty sure Take-Two would rather not have to deal with. I also wonder whether it will prompt Take-Two to release GTA 6 on PC more rapidly than it has with previous releases. A rumor to that effect surfaced in October and I had serious doubts, but it's possible that ongoing emulation efforts will expedite its arrival..

"We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of 8:00 PM (PDT) on Wednesday, September 29, 2027.".

Exoprimal launched on Xbox Series X|S on July 14, 2023, and suffered a pretty pants opening with only 4,995 players logging in through Steam to play Capcom's new team-based shooter.

It's still a fun title though, which makes the end of service announcement quite sad, at least for me.

Breaking: "Everyone agrees it's more fun this way": Toby Fox won't tell his team how Deltarune ends until they've built enough of it

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that toby Fox is a purposefully mysterious person.
  • Industry observers note that earlier this week, the fall edition of the Deltarune newsletter went out, offering a brief revision on the game's next and sixth chapter.
  • But in typical tricky Tony fashion, there's an upgrade for chapter seven where he makes it sound like no one but him knows how the whole game is going to end.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that toby Fox is a purposefully mysterious person. It was probably a wise choice on his part, obfuscating his current appearance with everyone's favourite annoying dog, essentially never speaking aloud in livestreams and instead using a text-to-speech bot, and posting only when there's notable enough Deltarune updates of if it would be very funny. But as it turns out, that sense of mystery extends to the team that's making Deltarune too, as Fox won't tell his devs how the game ends until they've built enough of it.

Industry observers note that earlier this week, the fall edition of the Deltarune newsletter went out, offering a brief revision on the game's next and sixth chapter. That one's apparently now a "structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end," but that doesn't mean it's quite ready for release, as "some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation." I'd expect a 2027 release for this chapter, which is going to be a shorter one too.

But in typical tricky Tony fashion, there's an upgrade for chapter seven where he makes it sound like no one but him knows how the whole game is going to end. "Well, we've only just started…," he explains of the progress. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way.".

I'm glad they all think it's fun, the wait for me personally certainly ain't. I do wonder if this speaks to a certain anxiety over how the game will shape up. Following the release of chapter five I was subjected to all manner of theories about what's to come by my partner gorging on YouTube videos from folks who mostly just seem quite excited about it all, even if a lot of them sound wrong. So I imagine there must be a little bit of weight to all of those varying expectations.

Fox did note in the newsletter that "unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!" so perhaps I'm speaking a load of hogwash! That said, I'm furious that a character called Apple Girlington didn't make it into chapter five, so you can expect to hear from my lawyers, Mr. Fox.

GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (442 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent.
  • According to recent reports, but that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear.
  • Industry observers note that "After the significant day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

According to recent reports, but that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

Industry observers note that "After the significant day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It states a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Rockstar's UK studios are right now voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more.".

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

As popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the firm has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

#121308. How to get abducted and find aliens in GTA 6

How to get abducted and find aliens in GTA 6

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (991 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The GTA 6 alien mission starts with an abduction that leads to some weird dreams, and eventually sends you off to literally find what's out there.
  • To start everything off you first need to be abducted.
  • According to recent reports, follow the cars headlights and you should see some clothes scattered around.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The GTA 6 alien mission starts with an abduction that leads to some weird dreams, and eventually sends you off to literally find what's out there. Spoilers obviously abound for everything I'm about to tell you below, but if you want to see what the latest instalment of Grand Theft Auto's alien stuff is, read on.

To start everything off you first need to be abducted. There's an element of luck here but what you're looking is to see a car by the side of the road with all its doors open and lights going crazy. It seems like there might be a few locations it can happen, and it can only happen at night, but for me it was here in Port Gellhorn:.

According to recent reports, follow the cars headlights and you should see some clothes scattered around. Using your flashlight and Focus you'll see more clothes making a trail you can follow. Eventually you'll see a light, and pick up something... else with your Focus. I won't spoil it too much:.

Once this sequence plays out you'll get the objective to go back to the woman's car. This is what triggers your own abduction experience. Once that's done you'll wake up by the side of the road apparently unharmed.

According to recent reports, to continue the GTA 6 alien quest you'll need to go to sleep to trigger some dreams. It might take a day or two but keep sleeping and you should eventually have some strange dreams. It needs to be the same character that was abducted, obviously, in case you're not seeing anything happen.

This dream is actually an explainer on how to rescue an alien, although there's a tricky puzzle to get past first.

Leaving the room you woke up in will take you to a large dark room full of eggs with a bright light at the center. The eggs will explode if you get too close, and once a few have popped you'll be grabbed by a tentacle. This will restart the dream with the option to 'give up', but don't. If you're having trouble all you need to do is sneak past slowly. If you crouch and keep your speed as low as possible you shouldn't pop any eggs, no matter how angry they look.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

You'll need to find a path through the eggs as it's a bit of a maze, but as long you move low and slow you should be able to reach the light in the middle easily, which will end this sequence.

Industry observers note that once past the alien eggs you'll reach a room with a model solar system in it. The Earth is actually a picture of a location, so examine that and move on.

Industry observers note that next you'll see a keypad with a series of lines over it. These lines denote the alien key pad code and are randomised. For me it was 3214 but you might have something different.

Don't worry about memorising it, as it will be noted like the GTA 6 safe codes you can find elsewhere. Once you're through you'll find a control panel to use. Switch it on and you'll see four buttons you'll need to turn green:.

Industry observers note that pushing any button will cycle the light either side of it through off, orange and then green. Using that info you'll need to make all the lights green and then press another button to reveal three doors ahead of you.

Recent findings suggest that through to door on the left you'l find some milk to fetch, and through the door on the right you'll find a machine you can put the milk in. The door in the middle has a burning sun inside that will kill you. We don't open the middle door.

According to recent reports, get the milk and take it to the machine. Placing it in the slot will then end this whole sequence and you'll wake up.

The radio tower you saw in your dream is at the location shown on the map above - just above Shoeless Keys. Drive there and use your car to encourage the gates to open, as there's barbed wire everywhere. Go around the building to this door and head inside:.

Immediately inside you'll see some stairs down to a door locked with a keypad. Use the code you got in your dream to open it. This will then take you down via lift to a control room where you'll find a tape you can play on a table, and then repeat what you learned in the dream:.

Putting the milk in the machine will open the door and reveal the alien. However, make sure you have full health before you pick it up. The second you grab the ET poison gas will start flooding the place, and you'll need to get to the lift as fast as possible while your health drains.

Head outside and let the events play out. When it's all over you'll have your health, stamina and focus all permanently increased. For reasons your car will probably be impounded and end up at the police station nearest your current home.

Sources indicate that if you are miles from home at this point, simply switch to the other character and then call up and arrange to meet. This will teleport whoever was stranded immediately back to you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s kind of hard to believe that Vanna White has been co-hosting Wheel of Fortune for nearly 45 years as of the 2026 television schedule. For thousands of episodes, White has been turning the iconic letter on the show, but her beginning was as humble as you would expect. In a recent appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, White told the story of her audition, why she was chosen by legendary producer Merv Griffin, and even what her first puzzle was (and the first letter she turned).

Of the audition process, White explained:.

Merv Griffin, God bless him. He chose me…. [There were] over 200 girls. And I said to him, ‘Why did you choose me?’ He said, ‘You turn the letters better than anyone else.’.

I mean, yeah, fair enough, right? Though White’s role on the show has grown a lot over the years, far beyond only turning (now touching) the letters (and working hard for her salary). In those early days, that was the job. If you’re going to get the gig, you better be elegant when you are flipping those lit-up boxes around! No one can argue with Griffin’s logic, and almost five incredible decades later, it's clear he couldn’t have made a better choice.

Speaking of turning letters, Fallon follows up White’s story about getting the job on Wheel by asking her if she remembers her first puzzle, and despite thousands of puzzles since, she does:.

It was ‘General Hospital,’ and my first letter was a T.

According to White, she’d wanted to be a TV star since she first saw her “uncle,” actor Christopher George, in an episode of his show The Rat Patrol in the mid ‘60s. George, it should be noted, was not a biological uncle, but was a close friend of her mother’s. On her first day filming, however, she was still quite nervous (and was even worried it wouldn't work out in the early days), telling Fallon:.

According to recent reports, I was so nervous. Oh my gosh. My teeth were [chattering], I couldn’t even talk. I was like, ‘Oh my gosh, is this really happening?’.

Sources indicate that famously, that wasn't the first time appearing on a game show. Two years before getting the job, she appeared as a contestant on The Price Is Right. Fallon and White talked about that appearance, which, sadly, ended without her making it on stage with Bob Barker, as she was never closest to the price of the item while on contestants' row.

White's first episode of Wheel aired on December 13, 1982, which means we’re just a couple of weeks away from her 44th anniversary. Pat Sajak was her co-host, of course, and the duo would work together for the next 42 years before Sajak retired from the show in 2024. She continues to co-host with Ryan Seacrest and has shown no signs of slowing down as she approaches 70 years old.

Wheel of Fortune airs daily across the country and can be streamed with a Peacock subscription.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a new breakthrough coming to light in recent days. The latest discovery? An elusive new cat that can be tamed by hunters in one of the game's new zones.

Recent findings suggest that the cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal. An endgame levelling zone, players will have to reach at least level 57 in order to safely make their way up there and recruit this new pet.

Sources indicate that the way you do so is relatively simple. You need to find a small corrupted cat figuring within the Felblood Scar region of Mount Hyjal. Once you've found that, you then need to travel up to a hidden lantern south of the Mourning's Rest area. With the figurine in your bags, you'll be able to interact with the lantern, spawning the cat for you to tame (granted you're playing a hunter).

Industry observers note that so what's the major deal about this cat? Well, aside from the fact it's got a strange colour scheme of green fur with orange stripes, the cat also has a base attack speed of 1.0. This means it'll attack once every second, which is pretty fast and allows for greater damage output from your pet. This inherently makes the pet valuable for endgame hunter players, who are looking to improve their performance in PvE and PvP.

In a recent development, this is not the only secret discovered by World of Warcraft: Forever sleuths. Last week, they pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. As of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among newly introduced and returning players. It's the biggest launch in the series' history, and has gone down well with people so far. Even if it has recently suffered its first controversy with a now-fixed gold exploit.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Many are asking themselves how a legendary studio like BioWare, which is responsible for staples of the PC gaming genre like Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and the OG Baldur's Gate, alongside Mass Effect and Dragon Age, can be shuttered.
  • Sources indicate that former Dragon Age executive producer Mark Darrah has already explained how the studio was backed into a corner by EA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that "I think the version of BioWare that survives EA better is a version where we drop down to one franchise at a time, maybe just one franchise at all. Maybe we just carve SWTOR off and they become an independent studio within EA, because I don't know how what I'm about to say makes sense if you don't do that. But you ship Mass Effect, you ship Dragon Age, and then one of those wins—I hate this—one of those wins and then you just become a one-project studio. There are lots of studios within EA that did that and it didn't work—they still got murdered in their sleep, so maybe that doesn't work anyway." Via an interview with Pembridge.

Many are asking themselves how a legendary studio like BioWare, which is responsible for staples of the PC gaming genre like Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and the OG Baldur's Gate, alongside Mass Effect and Dragon Age, can be shuttered.

Sources indicate that former Dragon Age executive producer Mark Darrah has already explained how the studio was backed into a corner by EA. Escalating financial pressure led to the poor decisions and subpar games we saw ahead of BioWare's closure. But what if it had all gone differently? Despite everything, Darrah does question whether there was a way for BioWare to survive under EA.

Industry observers note that "BioWare's entire existence under EA—it was essentially zero sum, if somebody was getting resources it was coming at the expense of somebody else," Darrah explains. "It's almost like BioWare has run exactly the same way for its entire existence. But the external constraints were different. So in the early days when BioWare needed more people it hired more people. That's like Baldur's Gate 1, Neverwinter Nights, in the early days when we have all these different threads and branches.

"And then in 2007/2008, when the EA constraints come in, the same desires are there, we need more people to ship our games so the way we fix that in that time period is by cutting off all those other branches. So [Jade Empire sequel] Revolver goes away and the Handheld [Development] Group goes away … and so Dragon Age and Mass Effect eats everything.".

Sources indicate that the alternative? Scaling things down to meet EA's needs. "Budgets keep going up, but we're still not getting bigger… So what's happening is that the walls are closing in and we're trying to be three things [SWTOR, Mass Effect, Dragon Age] and arguably we can only afford to be two things, or one thing." There's no telling whether this would've saved BioWare, but it has worked for other studios.

"Maxis figured out how to live inside of EA and BioWare never did," Darrah adds. Focusing on just one project does seem to be the answer, or at least Darrah believes it has been for Maxis and Battlefield Studios, which both had games that initially underperformed and weren't well received. "If [Battlefield Studios] don't work on Battlefield then you might as well shut the studio down. So they all work on Battlefield 4 and they fix Battlefield 4 and it becomes successful, like very successful after the fact. The Sims 4, same thing.".

Industry observers note that on the other hand "Mass Effect Andromeda ships and then Dragon Age 4 which has been starving for resources is like 'No, no [the devs] are supposed to come to us. Where are they?' That need to keep them in place isn't there in the same way. So when I say BioWare didn't adapt to EA, that's what I mean.".

These agreements cover the presence of CDPR games on subscription services such as PlayStation Plus, but also "our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign" - which is the bit we're particularly interested in.

Here's a bit of the transcription via our friends at VGC:.

"Just today, we signed new partnership agreements with Sony Interactive Entertainment covering the presence of our games on PlayStation and in PlayStation Plus subscriptions, as well as our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign.".

"This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years.".

A lot of people are now speculating that The Witcher 4's "collaboration" with Sony may be akin to what Take-Two has done with GTA 6, pushing the whole "plays best on PS5" campaign and restricting how Xbox is allowed to advertise the game. For example, GTA's launch trailer was solely focused around PS5 for an exclusive window.

It's crucial to highlight that this is just speculation though, and there may be aspects of these agreements that aren't exclusive at all. We've seen CDPR titles like Cyberpunk 2077 on Xbox Game Pass in the not too distant past, for example, so the PlayStation Plus agreement doesn't necessarily mean Game Pass is out the window.

Let's wait and see what happens with this, but just keep in mind that we could be looking at a situation where The Witcher 4 gets a bigger push on PlayStation than Xbox when it (hopefully) releases in 2028. We'll also leave you with a fun GTA comparison quote from joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski about the difference between Witcher 3 and 4!

Sources indicate that "I’m not going to make a deep dive, full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6, but of course, we did look at the game, we did see the differences... we believe there’s going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs.
  • In an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend.
  • These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

In an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop.".

These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

Cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their intends. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying latest," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition.".

According to recent reports, though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

Industry observers note that of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony aims to stop producing physical discs for latest PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

Industry observers note that disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • 🌕NIGHT EYE TV’s initial form is live!🌑 Check out the site and follow our Indiegogo campaign at www.nighteye.tv![image or embed].
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I am both a bit too young and a bit too very not American to have ever experienced public-access television, but it's something that's always fascinated me. For those too young to have even heard of it, or just not in the know, it essentially allowed anyone to broadcast their own reveals through cable TV. A proto YouTube, if you will. It's obviously not what it was any more, given the advent of the internet, but in NIGHTEYE.TV, it may be making a digital, more interactive return.

NIGHTEYE.TV is a strange little place. I call it a place, it's a fake TV floating in a Unity default texture void, lending it a Backroomsian vibe, but even if there's not much there to ground yourself in, the goggle box is enticing all the same. It beckons you to turn it on, a series of buttons all linking to different "channels." What awaits you isn't television, however. Instead you'll find games, mostly of the weirdo, freako, sicko variety, rapidly setting the tone.

🌕NIGHT EYE TV’s initial form is live!🌑 Check out the site and follow our Indiegogo campaign at www.nighteye.tv![image or embed].

In its current incarnation, it's mostly just a collection of clips of these various art games, with direct links to them hidden away in a menu, but a good collection it is. You'll find Nathalie Lawhead's Everything is Going to Be OK, Jeremy Couillard's more recent Soul Injector Commando, and Taylor McCue's He Fucked The Girl Out Of Me. Some clips are longer than others, acting as sort of segments of playthroughs, but it all feels like an exciting evolution of what public-access television was.

According to recent reports, the ultimate goal is for it to be a curated platform where you can buy a rotating selection of games. Most of the sale goes back to the original artist, and 15% gets put into a community pool to be split amongst all of the contributors, with the last 15% going towards keeping everything running. As it stands, that's not quite ready yet. You can help make it happen, though, as right now an Indiegogo campaign is running to help it all get fully operational. Worth chucking a few quid I reckon!

In a recent development, the fastest cars in GTA 6 tend to be incredibly expensive, but you can actually get some for free if you're strategic and know where to look. The fastest car is the Thrax Truffade owned by Andrew Node, a modified version of the standard supercar, but there's other options out there that are a little more reliable. Below I'll lay out all the fastest cars in Grand Theft Auto 6 and how you can get them for yourself.

The top 5 fastest cars in GTA 6 are as follows:.

Keep in mind that there's basically no real speed difference between the Progen Emerus GTA 6 cars, they all come in joint equal for the silver medal, and the only real variation is how they look for the most part.

To get the fastest car in GTA 6 you need to get Andrew Node’s Thrax Truffade, a modified version of the standard Truffade that goes even faster. You can get this one for free at any point in the game by doing a certain glitch, though keep in mind that it's much easier after you've obtained the Key Cloner in GTA 6.

It has been revealed that andrew Node's Thrax Truffade is actually unregistered, meaning you can add it to your list of GTA 6 Personal Vehicles at any point. Though it will cost you $70,000 to do so, so make sure you've either built up your personal wealth, or have a garage to keep it in until that point.

You can find the Honeycomb Emerus in Vice City, in a parking lot outside a dealership and car rental spot across from the Hospital. This one is very easy to access – it's basically just outside – but it does require a Key Cloner, and it has Advanced Security and Trackers. This is something you can't really make best use of until the mid-to-late game.

This one is found inside a shipping container at the location in the Vice City County Dockyard. Keep in mind that not only is it illegal for you to be here, you'll need to have unlocked the cut-off tool in GTA 6.

In a recent development, however, if you can reach the area, use Focus mode to identify the one shipping container you can open, evade or KO the nearby security, and use the cut-off tool to get inside. This car is actually unlocked and deactivated – though registering it will cost you $29,900. You'll also need to quickly drive it out of the dockyard to avoid getting arrested and shot to pieces.

According to recent reports, you can find the Seaspray inside a garage in Northwest Capri. You can unlock the garage with the Snap Gun in GTA 6, and again, it has all the most advanced car security features. Still, it's very easy to physically get to the car, to one to consider.

Recent findings suggest that the baseline Thrax Truffade is usually found on the back of a trailer at the entrance to the Boone Raceway in Southwest Hamlet, just outside of the entrance. Like the Seaspray and Honeycomb, it's dripping with security features, so you won't be able to keep it until the later stages of the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The buzziest film on the 2026 movie schedule has to be You Can See Everything, and it just hit a major milestone by crossing the $100 million mark at the box office. For a movie that was made for a reported $7 million, it’s certainly one of the most successful A24 releases ever, but the Elizabeth Holmes documentary is nowhere close to the top-grossing documentary of all time, worldwide. That record belongs to the King of Pop himself for the posthumously released Michael Jackson: This Is It from 2009. How does it stack up to other documentaries? Well, it depends on how you count things.

It has been revealed that anyway you count, in terms of worldwide gross, This Is It sits at the top of the list, with almost $268 million, according to Box Office Mojo. Second on the list is Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour, which made $261 million worldwide, and most of it ($180 million) in the United States. Both far outpace Fahrenheit 9/11, which is third on the list and the first non-music documentary. The Michael Moore-directed movie about the lead-up to the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq was a box office sensation from the moment it was released.

It has been revealed that you Can See Everything wasn’t quite the rocket ship that Fahrenheit 9/11 was out of the box, but it did a ton of steady business for weeks, finally topping the weekend box office in its third week of release. Now, after its release in the United Kingdom, the Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim-directed documentary has joined rarefied air as a documentary hitting that milestone. The $100 million mark slots You Can See Everyone into 7th worldwide.

Industry observers note that nature documentaries litter the top ten, with the IMAX-exclusive Everest, (filmed during the disastrous season on the mountain in 1996) coming in fourth all time, Earth coming in at #6 on the list (Penguins is 5th), and Oceans is 9th. The other slots in the top ten are both music-related: Justin Bieber: Never Say Never (8th) and One Direction: This Is Us (10th).

Here are the top ten-grossing documentaries of all time (worldwide), along with their gross, according to Box Office Mojo:.

Sources indicate that that means the only two non-music and non-nature documentaries in the top ten are Fahrenheit 9/11 and You Can See Everything. It also means that You Can See Everything won’t be catching up to Michael Jackson. I don’t expect You Can See Everything to improve significantly at the worldwide box office. Elizabeth Holmes may be fascinating and infamous here, but Jackson was a massive star in every corner of the globe. In fact, domestically, This Is It actually trails You Can See Everything by almost $20 million.

It has been revealed that it’s the domestic numbers that really tell you the story of just how buzzy the film is, as it ranks 3rd all time at U.S. box offices, behind Fahrenheit 9/11 and The Eras Tour. It also has a very good chance of separating itself from the pack as the first documentary nominated for Best Picture at the Oscars, something not even March of the Penguins did. Who knows, maybe it will be competing against this year's Michael in that category.

Latest Update: Alt Video is a digital, faux Blockbuster video store that you can fill with movies from your Letterboxd watchlist and Plex server

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films.
  • This is, obviously, not so dissimilar to Boxroom, a game where you can design your own bedroom that lets you use your Steam profile to fill it with games you actually own.
  • According to recent reports, alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films. I know this, because over the past few years, I've become one of those people… a Letterboxd user. Gasp! I know, I know, but I don't think I'm too insufferable about it. I'll only do a joke review in the hopes of like farming if I think it's genuinely funny! But many of these films were watched digitally, meaning I don't have a bunch of DVDs to admire on a shelf. So what am I to do? Well, I could check out Alt Video, a not quite job simulator where you can use your Letterboxd account or media server to fill up a digital, faux Blockbuster.

This is, obviously, not so dissimilar to Boxroom, a game where you can design your own bedroom that lets you use your Steam profile to fill it with games you actually own. With Alt Video, you do things slightly differently just because of the focus on a different format. So, say you have a Letterboxd account. After exporting some data from your account, you can bring that into Alt Video, and this fake video store will then get filled up with shelves of DVD cases of all the films you've watched.

According to recent reports, alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store. What's more interesting here is that there's a cinema room in the store that lets you watch films on your Plex server, and it's possible to invite your Steam friends to watch along with you. There's even a few other rooms, like a '90s bedroom or family room for more of a CRT kinda vibe. It's cute! If you like you can even manually add any DVDs or Blu-rays you own to appear on all the shelves too.

There's a lot of other nice touches too. In the case of your Letterboxd data, your ratings even show up on the back of the boxes. It's not just relegated to films either, you can put in highlights or even your games. The whole thing can be played in VR if you really want that immersive feel. There's a store clerk who can give you some recommendations if you're not sure what to watch. And there's even a day and night system, weather, and seasonal shopfront facelifts.

According to recent reports, alt Video is currently slated for release next week on November 24th, and it'll be doing so in early access. Worth noting that for now the focus is on the browsing, but features involving serving customers and running the store are on the way. You can wishlist it on Steam right here.

GTA 6 has replaced websites with social media and phone apps because "it didn't feel necessary"

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (469 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.
  • Industry observers note that the web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps.
  • "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.

Industry observers note that the web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps. The reason? Smartphone apps just made more sense.

"It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps.".

Though some of the apps in GTA 6 perform similar tasks to the web of old, Nelson mentioned the team didn't want players to be distracted from the game's detailed open world by staring at screens. That also extends to getting players to appreciate the value of money, and witnessing the progression of Jason and Lucia as they go from pawnshop robberies to staging major bank heists.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," Nelson mentioned, adding that websites may return in the future.

In a recent development, "I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it," he added.

In materials supplied by Rockstar ahead of our review, Sam Grosset (associate UI director at the studio) also explained that a lot of thought went into how the apps work, and how easily the phone needed to fit into your play style in order for it to work as effectively as possible.

Sources indicate that "We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so," said Grosset. "The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario. It was a big shift for our phone interface to be in-hand, but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world.".

Rockstar would continually "raise the bar, question assumptions, explore newly introduced possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration" in order to make these apps - and the UX/UI in general - feel in line with the production quality of the rest of the game.

In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, Chris Tapsell awarded the open-world crime game five stars, raving about its absurd level of detail, compelling characters, exciting action and of its significant heart.

If you're looking to spend the next several days playing Rockstar's latest hit, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough has detailed guides on everything from individual missions, to core mechanics like the fresh Wanted Level, and relationship and romance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in my first 30 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6, I think I saw it rain once. And that was during a particularly gloomy main story mission where it felt like it was intentionally flipped on and not a serendipitous moment created by the game's weather system.

In a recent development, I was not alone in wondering what was up with the weather in Leonida. GTA 6 players have been confused by the lack of rain and fog since day one, especially after Rockstar boasted about the kind of storms and hurricanes it can create to Game Informer in September.

Apparently, the questioning was justified: The weather system was broken and should now be fixed in a upcoming patch that went out today.

"Fixed an matter that resulted in weather not changing for extended periods," the patch notes say, confirming that, while some players witnessed changes in weather, it was not properly happening at the rate it was intended.

You don't partner with The Weather Channel to post exclusive pre-release screenshots of your game if the forecast is mostly sunny and not actually representative of Florida, the state with the most unpredictable weather in the US. GTA 6 has realistically detailed radio towers that left a TikTok guy who's worked on them in real life gobsmacked. It would've been bizarre if Rockstar neglected to put that kind of effort into a system normies like me would notice within a few hours.

According to recent reports, the sun's reign is over and all the other meteorological conditions can take the spotlight. As someone who takes their time doing all the silly little daily routines in Jason and Lucia's life and abiding by traffic laws for the vibes, I'm excited to see how much the weather affects the mood. I'll just have to remember to be a little more discerning when chasing down one of GTA 6's cars to make sure I don't absolutely ruin the interior from a surprise storm.

It has been revealed that this is a zombie apocalypse game that served as one of the most successful examples of a proper single-player FPS in the early VR era, first releasing all the way back in 2016. It's obviously received a lot of changes for the Xbox release, most notably in the form of a newly introduced third-person perspective rather than sticking with first-person.

Its story focuses around a survivor called "Sunny" and his dog known as "Buddy", the latter of which is now playable in two-player co-op as of this newly introduced release. Don't be fooled by Buddy's cuteness though - it's still a gory game and certainly not intended for kids, so just keep that in mind before you hit the purchase button or the trailer up above!

Anyway, Arizona Sunshine was a big deal 10 years ago, so it'll be fascinating to see how well it fares on modern non-VR platforms. The game is already available to pre-order on the Xbox Store at a low price of £21.99 / $24.99, and it also seemingly comes with Xbox Play Anywhere support (meaning you get a free PC copy too).

We'll leave you with more details on Arizona Sunshine below, launching for Xbox on January 21st of 2027.

According to recent reports, sharpen your machete and grab your friends. Arizona Sunshine® brings its award-winning zombie apocalypse to explosive third-person action, featuring online and split-screen co-op, brutal combat, dark humor, and Buddy, your loyal zombie-chomping canine companion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other significant-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

Sources indicate that that's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

Industry observers note that however, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:.

Away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were new releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a big slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:.

Industry observers note that in Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything new, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you want to enjoy 8K polling gaming accessories on your PC, you can usually have to pay a bit of a premium, even with some comparatively affordable options hitting the market this year. But thanks to Amazon's Black Friday deals, you can save a lot of money on one of our go-to picks.

Industry observers note that the GameSir G7 Pro 8K PC is down to $63.99 at Amazon, saving you 20% on its asking price, and marking the first serious discount for this controller since its launch earlier in the year. Some of the controller's various special editions are also reduced, but it's the standard model which is enjoying the best discount. If you've been tempted by an 8K polling controller, this deal is the one to jump on to experience what it's like.

Industry observers note that the GameSir G7 Pro 8K hasn't seen a seriously good price cut just yet, since it was released at the beginning of the year, and this non-Special-Edition model later still. So this is almost undoubtedly the best price you'll get on this 8K polling controller for a while.

Industry observers note that there are several models of the GameSir G7 Pro 8K, and the standard black or white model, like the one above, is the cheapest. There are some alternative versions though: the Phantom Blade Zero edition, Aimlabs Edition, and Nioh 3 edition are all down to $71.99. There's also a Royal2 model down to $67.49. Other than the themes changing the color options, though, there's no difference in how they work.

It has been revealed that now, if you're looking for a new controller for a console, let me stop you right here: until the GameSir G7 Pro, the 8K model only works on PC. This ain't gonna play GTA 6 any time soon, that's for sure.

In a recent development, the point of 8K polling is that the controller picks up your inputs more times per second, leading to more accurate gameplay. This is useful if you value your precision. For example, if you play lots of online multiplayer games, GameSir is pitching it as a controller for Esports. When I tested the G7 Pro 8K, it spent a lot of time on Arc Raiders; that's the kind of title it's best suited to.

The flip side is that 8K peripherals are going to really suit you and your gameplay if you play at higher frame rates. Moreover, you're going to need a motherboard and USB port that can make the most of those higher speeds; otherwise, this kind of controller might not be worth it for you. If you've been putting off an internals upgrade for a few too many years, maybe check that your motherboard and USB ports are compatible with an 8K controller.

It has been revealed that that doesn't mean you need the latest RTX model, though. The graphics card isn't going to have a say in how your controller functions, so no need to worry about looking for GPU discounts that don't exist right now. I used the controller loads on my road to 100%ing Nioh 3, and it mostly worked totally fine on my RTX 3060 Ti.

If you're looking to use the regular 1,000Hz polling rate, or you want to play on Xbox, the GameSir G7 Pro is reduced down to $63.99, and might be a better buy.

In a recent development, we've got a large list of all the Black Friday gaming deals you should be aware of, in case there are more deals out there. You can also read our round-up of the best PC controller for gaming, to see competitors.

According to recent reports, fans who spent years watching the Marvel movies in order are gearing up for the shared universe's next major crossover event with Avengers: Doomsday. Arguably the most anticipated upcoming Marvel movie in years, the blockbuster has been steadily building excitement since those teasers arrived back in January. Now Joe Russo explained why they decided to give us footage that early.

Recent findings suggest that we recently got the final Doomsday trailer, which instantly went viral thanks to epic moments from Cyclops and Steve Rogers. What we know about Avengers: Doomsday is still limited, but the excitement building around the movie has been steadily building for months. While at Qatar Film Committee’s second Doha Industry Days (via Deadline) Russo spoke about this unique marketing strategy, offering:.

Sources indicate that I have to work extra hard to subvert your expectations and be aware of who you are as a viewer and how you’re changing. The last time I did this, in 2018, 2019, is very different than now because we’ve been through a pandemic; lots of people spent a lot of time on social media. The industry has changed a bit since Endgame arrived in theaters, and the MCU has had a number of box office blunders including bombs like The Marvels. As such, The Russos wanted get the hype train running early, with more news, casting, and footage methodically released to the public.

Later in the same appearance, Russo went on to share how audiences have changed over the years. As such Endgame followed the chairs casting announcement with four exciting teasers. As he put it:.

Recent findings suggest that I have to interact with the fans in order to understand what is moving them, what is working for them. What we’ve been doing with Doomsday is very different than the last time we did this because the speed of conversation on the internet is even faster than it was in 2018, 2019. I had this idea, why don’t we start the story a year early? Why don’t we start dropping clues in the year leading up to the movie… we did four trailers that were sprinkled out.

Those brief clips rapidly went viral, especially the Captain America teaser that confirmed Chris Evans was returning as Steve Rogers. With the next Avengers movie now just a few weeks away from its release, anticipation has reached a fever pitch that should (hopefully) result in massive box office numbers. Perhaps future MCU projects will follow this same strategy.

Recent findings suggest that we'll find out shortly as Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list. Marvel might be in for a one-two punch, as Spider-Man: Brand Upcoming Day broke Endgame's box office record just a few months ago.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that an upgrade for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications.
  • Sources indicate that the Repentance+ update went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that an upgrade for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications. This free addition to the Repentance+ version of the roguelike featured a Grand Terry Auto-inspired daily run, complete with cops, guns, and a soundtrack players soon highlighted as sounding AI-generated. Sure enough, Nicalis subsequently announced the "removal of generated music files" in response to the backlash.

Sources indicate that the Repentance+ update went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st. In the interim, a Reddit user with the handle ShweetsStuff unearthed metadata pointing to AI tune generator Suno attached to some of the update's music files. Cue understandable questioning of why the DLC's Steam page hadn't had a disclosure of this genAI use slapped across it.

Original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have quickly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action. "Woke up to a shit show," he posted on the former Twitterverse on the 21st. Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.".

Recent findings suggest that given the fresh build yanking the music went live later that day, McMillen's voice maybe only added to the chorus of complaints Nicalis were already aware of and facing. Either way, the songs are gone and Nicalis don't look to have said anything as of writing about whether they'll be replaced at some point down the line.

This isn't the first time a developer has considered using AI to generate songs designed to satirise or parody. In the case of Future? No Thanks! dev Paolo 'Molleindustria' Pedercini, the aim was partly to poke fun at disclosures, with people in the game's future society listening to AI-generated tunes that're corporately mandated to mention AI in the lyrics. Pedercini ended up deciding not to use AI-generated music in the final release.

On the face of it, while the effectiveness of using AI-generated songs to parody AI-generated songs is questionable, the argument for it seems stronger in a more focused satire like Future? No Thanks! than in the case of The Binding of Isaac having a GTA 6-related giggle. I've not listened to the Repentance+ enhancement's AI tunes, but there's nothing obvious to indicate that their satirical job wouldn't have been done as well or better by Nicalis commissioning or otherwise employing someone to pen some entirely human-made ditties, that spoofed the nature of Large Stealy Wheely.

Perhaps the publishers will now go and do just that.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end.
  • The case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights.
