📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Obviously, massive spoilers follow for GTA 6 endings!

There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and while we haven't experienced them all personally here at PC Gamer, the gaming community has been sharing them around for anyone curious about what they may have missed.

The ending you get depends on the choices you make during the final GTA 6 story mission, but also depends on how you handled Jason and Lucia's romance and criminal profiles throughout the game, so seeing every version of the ending would mean not just playing the ending multiple times, but having different playthroughs of the game altogether.

It has been revealed that there are a couple of endings that I don't consider "different" from each other but do have some differences leading up to them, which I'll explain below. There may also be additional endings we haven't seen yet, so we may update this guide in the future.

In the bridge endings, Jason and Lucia have defeated Mendez and his squad and gotten the hard drive back from Georgio's penthouse and escaped. They drive to Cal's place in Key Lento, but discover he has been compromised. They drive to the bridge, but the cops have set up a roadblock and have the couple trapped. Lucia wants to keep going, but Jason suggests they jump off the bridge and swim for it.

A choice comes up on the screen: "Swim For it" or "No Surrender.".

Industry observers note that jason and Lucia try to run the roadblock and are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, we see that their son Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, their lawyer, Abe, brings the money to Lucia's aunt. Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children in a much bigger house than the other No Surrender ending.

Choosing "Swim for it" presents an additional choice. When Jason gets out of the car, Lucia can choose to "Exit" the car with him, or change her mind by not choosing it.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. They both exit the car without holding guns. Lucia jumps, but Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Lucia signs a deal for immunity while Jason goes to prison. Lucia gets a job in a diner. Lucia takes Tomas to meet Jason in prison, but he can only see his son through a glass divider.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. Jason exits the car with a gun, but Lucia changes her mind and stays in the car. The police open fire and Jason and Lucia are both shot to death. Tomas lives with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Recent findings suggest that jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it, Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Two years later, Lucia uses the savings account to get Jason freed from prison. Lucia goes to the prison to pick up Jason. Jason meets Tomas and holds his hand.

If you don't have a strong relationship between Jason and Lucia, there is a different ending location: the base of Georgio's tower. In these endings, the couple never makes it to the bridge. You can also choose to break up the couple, either as Jason or as Lucia, as you begin the mission Protective Custody.

After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront the couple at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia has a choice to "Stay down" or "Defend Jason". She stays down and watches Jason die. Lucia is arrested, signs a deal, and visits Tomas at her aunt's house. Lucia then leaves Tomas with her aunt, takes out a gun, and continues her life of crime by preparing to rob a diner.

According to recent reports, after the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront them at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia chooses "Defend Jason" and fights the cops. They die together.

On the way down to ground level at the tower, Jason decides to run. Lucia is arrested and signs the deal, then lives with her aunt and Tomas while working in a diner. One night there's a knock on the door and she finds a bag of cash on the porch. We see Jason driving away with... Rocco the drug-sniffing dog from earlier in the game. Sure, that might as well happen.

How to get this ending (sourced by GamingwithTZ on YouTube):.

It has been revealed that jason and Lucia make a deal with Mendez after defeating him. Once they have the hard drive, they're surrounded by cops at the bottom of the tower. Mendez arrives and takes them away in his car, then drives them to the swamp. Later in the credits, we see two skulls in the swamp, side-by-side, with a bullet hole in each.

According to recent reports, note: You may need a specific criminal profile for this ending. I tried to take the deal (as Lucia) in one of my ending playthroughs, but Jason shot Mendez anyway. I had both Jason and Lucia at "Professional" level criminal profiles. This ending was not available to me. Speculation, but this ending may only be available if you don't have "Professional" as your criminal profiles.

There are potentially (and almost certainly) more endings to GTA 6. There are still a few combinations of all the different variables, including your romance level, criminal profile level, amount of money saved, and the choices you make during the final mission, that we haven't seen yet.

We'll enhancement this guide if the community finds more endings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Literal decades ago, I tried to make a first-person RPG in HyperCard. I got as far as a fateful town gate confrontation before hitting the cap on slides for the shareware version. I mention this because fresh, 100% "hand-drawn" first-person dungeon crawler Rise of Furax is uncannily redolent of my long-lost HyperCard game.

Industry observers note that this risks being a) a terrible indictment of the game's visual direction, and b) an insinuation that developers Rap2h are dastardly rip-off artists, so let me elaborate that c) I think Rise of Furax looks far, far lovelier than my lousy primordial hypermedia confection and d) it is a legally distinct creation. That unfinished HyperCard concept never left the confines of a Macintosh Performa that is even now rusting on a riverbed. If only I'd pitched it somewhere, I'd probably be a MILLIONAIRE by now. A million pounds is still a lot of money, right? Anyway, here's a teaser video for Rise of Furax.

Sources indicate that the plot setup here is thusly: some apocalypse cult is raising havoc on three islands off the coast of Rivelune. Five heroes – a snake minstrel, a rhino barbarian, a badger knight, a goat sorcerer and… whatever the hell critter that monk is - have been sent to investigate the whole "world is ending" sheebang and do a little levelling.

As in the very first Might and Magic, you steer the party as one, moving around a grid map. Combat is turn-based and there are "secrets, puzzles, and hidden items everywhere". Also schmürpfs. These confuse me even more than the monk character. They look like angry green omelettes. Any pointers? I googled the word and the closest match I could find was Swiss footballer Pascal Schürpf, who appears neither green nor egg-based.

"Every element, from sprites to textures, was hand-drawn on paper," promises the Steam page. It's out April 2027. There's no demo as yet nor even a proper trailer, but god I enjoyed looking at this, in a week otherwise full of screenshots of, like, suggestive scallion distribution in GTA 6. I should finish that HyperCard game. I still remember which river I threw the Performa into.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Skate, the free-to-play skateboarding game that's still in Early Access, is ditching its seasonal approach moving forward, publisher EA has confirmed.

The always-online, shared world game has been getting fairly regular updates since its launch back in September 2025, and it's all been modelled around Seasons. Following the next patch — 0.33, launching 1st December — this system will be dropped.

No more Seasons also means no more Skate Passes or Tix; instead, the development team is prioritising "regular, agile content updates", saying it'll be able to launch features earlier and get active feedback from players:.

Industry observers note that "Moving away from rigid season blocks gives the development team the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle. This means we can deploy work-in-progress mechanics and gather your direct feedback to continuously shape and build upon San Vansterdam. We’ve started this with in-game testing of features such as Spot Battles, Block Parties, and Prox Chat before rolling it out officially, and we’re going to continue with this process to ensure we get YOUR feedback on what works/what doesn’t.".

On top of this incoming change, the game's next update is a fairly hefty one:.

Industry observers note that the competitive game mode S.K.A.T.E. is being added, with various spots on the map where you can play, or you can use the Throwdown menu to create your own challenges.

Another major feature in this patch is (optional) proximity chat, which will be available on all maps in the game.

For those that don't know, proximity chat is a version of voice chat that means you can only hear players that are close by.

Version 0.33 is also adding and updating locations in San Vansterdam, such as the RINQ Hotel, the Loading Bay of The Vault, and Pump House Park on the Isle of Grom.

On top of that, the patch introduces new cosmetics, music, and more.

Recent findings suggest that it seems there's a good amount to check out in the new enhancement. It'll be interesting to see how the game evolves now that it's discontinuing Seasons.

Industry observers note that are you still enjoying Skate on PS5? Tell us in the comments section below.

[source ea.com, via youtube.com].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that managing my car's gas and its engine health is latest for GTA 6 – part of a swathe of delightfully tactile mechanics that add to the immersion of Vice City and Leonida as true spaces. Which is my excuse for running so low on fuel I genuinely worry that I might grind to a halt when I'm meant to be picking up my 'it's complicated' girlfriend from her prison release program trash-cleaning job, um, (checks watch) by 4pm! What I don't have an excuse for is being clear out of cash, and not being able to pay to fill it up. Lucia, I'm sorry!

Industry observers note that for a guy in the drug trade, Jason really doesn't have a lot of dough – and I really feel it in GTA 6's early hours across Chapter One. Living rent free in a half-rotting house, any maintenance will have to be handled myself (while shirtless, sweat glistening in the Leonidan sun, of course). Having spent years post-military with no bank account, off the grid, I collect my illicit money from a mailbox, then stash it under the floorboards, weighing up how much to stow safely and how much actual cash to keep on my person – where it'll be easier to lose.

Recent findings suggest that after Lucia gets out of prison, we end up setting up a joint BuckMe account as well – a tenuous digital wallet that's our only option when we're rejected from getting a proper bank account. I can pay into our joint saving goals but can't withdraw from it, giving me a third money tracker on the UI that can only be used for certain other payments, with some jobs paying me directly into funds I can access via an ATM. What could feel annoying in other games is thematically and mechanically effective here – at least in the opening – as Jason is constantly reminded he's at the bottom of the food chain.

Industry observers note that with a more nuanced police wanted system, money can be more important than ever to simply surviving in a system looking to chew up Jason and Lucia at every turn. At one point, I attract too much heat in a neighborhood after a police cruiser zooms into my way across an intersection and I can't brake in time. And, yes, I kind of, sort of, then ran over several people.

With my face, appearance, and car popping up as elements now known by the police until the heat dies down, I have to ditch my ride and stick to alleys before I duck into a shop to hastily buy upcoming clothes before I boost another car to escape. Except, after one fancy hat too many I realize I'm down to ten bucks and can't buy new clothes. Shamefully, I buy a one-dollar chocolate bar and skulk back into the night.

As the plot accelerates, I try to find other ways to snag money so I can have a bigger money buffer to keep on-hand. Recovering drug drops after a delivery gone wrong, and free to handle the goods as I please, it's up to me to turn these bags of goods into money – just securing them isn't worth anything on its own. With a couple of options for who to sell them to, I notice even here Jason is open to getting ripped off, as each fence has their own unique going rate for narcotics (both 'low'). The higher paying one is a more unstable sort, liable to get me into trouble, while the other is ostensibly my boss' boss, who has already called me to complain about me being late to missions multiple times.

Whether its capital capital or social capital, Vice City and its surroundings are glitzy for the right people – but for those like Jason and Lucia, just trying to build a safe life for themselves while those on all sides of the law try to screw them over, Leonida is a power keg of pressure. When I can't even buy gas to pick up my girlfriend, I really feel it like in no GTA before.

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

"Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!".

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the fresh edition.

Since it rolled out on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

According to recent reports, another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2.

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard stated WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

Longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most upcoming players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

In a recent development, last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among fresh and returning players.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Deborah Ann Woll mentioned she felt "totally unbothered" by the small but vocal subset of gamers who were upset by the upcoming God of War: Laufey, and apparently she meant it—because today Amazon MGM Studios announced that she's going to play the same role in the live-action God of War series coming to Prime.

Just as in God of War: Laufey and its predecessor, God of War: Ragnarok, Woll—best known for playing Karen Page in Marvel's Daredevil, Defenders, and Punisher TV series, as well as a lengthy stint on True Blood as Jessica Hamby—will portray Faye, wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus.

"Faye’s abrupt passing sets in motion the events of God of War," the announcement says. "Along their journey, Kratos and Atreus discover secrets about Faye that make them wonder how well they truly knew her at all.".

It's been a bumpy road for the God of War series. It was first reported in 2022, but started over from scratch two years later after the showrunner and executive producers quit. We got our first look at Ryan Hurst as Kratos earlier this year—not very impressive, but we all had the same initial impression of Henry Cavill as Geralt and that worked out well—but then Hurst had to be recast because of an on-set injury; Dave Bautista now has the lead role. Child actors Callum Vinson and Island Austin, who played Atreus and Thrud, were also recast.

According to recent reports, god of War: Laufey is set to launch on May 20, 2027, but sadly is a PlayStation 5 exclusive, a state of affairs that seems likely to endure given Sony's recent strategy shift. The God of War live action series on Prime has been ordered for two seasons, but a release target hasn't been revealed.

Sorry, Unbeatable.

The iPhone Duo Is Getting Face Unlock

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (468 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't.
  • Apple is at the moment beta testing the third major patch in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure.
  • Industry observers note that with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that apple dropped iOS 27.2.1 last week, patching a handful of security vulnerabilities and bugs—including two iMessage flaws that let people read messages they shouldn't. But while most of us are running this version (or should install it as soon as possible), others are running something different—iOS 27.3.

Apple is at the moment beta testing the third major patch in the iOS 27 era, and anyone—developer and public tester alike—is free to install it at their leisure. With it, comes the return of the Health app, vertical Safari tabs, and Siri AI app actions, among other newly introduced features. But for customers of Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, iOS 27.3 brings two rather notable changes—both of which are for the better.

Industry observers note that with the second iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple is introducing face unlock for the iPhone Duo. The foldable famously ships with Touch ID, the first new iPhone since the third-gen iPhone SE to do so. While that isn't a problem per se, many of us are used to unlocking our iPhones with our faces. This enhancement just lets new Duo owners keep up with that muscle memory.

Industry observers note that now, take note: This isn't Face ID. No software enhancement can introduce new hardware, so the iPhone Duo still doesn't have the camera tech required to power Apple's Face ID system. As such, the Duo's face unlock is likely not as secure as Face ID on other iPhones. Perhaps that's why your iPhone Duo will require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. This feature seems to be one of pure convenience: If you want to be able to unlock your Duo with your face (at least, some of the time), you can.

It has been revealed that what's more, this isn't a default setting. If you're running the beta, or if you're reading this after iOS 27.3 drops, you can find the option in Settings > Touch ID & Passcode.

Industry observers note that apple made a significant deal about the continuity involved with opening and closing the iPhone Duo. As you do, your content moves with you seamlessly—a very Apple thing to do. That said, you might expect folding the Duo to lock it, but it doesn't. You need to hit the side button to actually put the phone to sleep.

iOS 27.3 changes that. If you so choose, you can enable a setting to lock your Duo whenever you close it. That won't work for everyone, of course—some users may still want to move between modes without worrying about locking their Duos. But for those who would rather lock their devices whenever they fold them up, the new option is under Settings > Display & Brightness.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I just watched the trailer for Netflix's upcoming The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey, which premieres as part of the 2026 TV schedule, and.
  • It has been revealed that the trailer begins on Dec.
  • In a recent development, the preview then moves into the investigation and the attention that followed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I just watched the trailer for Netflix's upcoming The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey, which premieres as part of the 2026 TV schedule, and. I'm left with a feeling of uneasiness. The trailer itself is surprisingly restrained, and Melissa McCarthy looks terrific as Patsy Ramsey, alongside Clive Owen as her husband, John. Nothing in the footage is particularly shocking, at least by the standards we've come to expect from the genre. Yet I finished watching it with a sinking feeling I haven't quite been able to shake.

It has been revealed that the trailer begins on Dec. 26, 1996, with McCarthy's Patsy making the frantic 911 call reporting that her daughter is missing. Police arrive at the Boulder, Colorado, house, and the family reveals them a ransom note. We know how the search ends: JonBenét is found dead in the basement. Watching actors retrace those hours, even briefly, made me uncomfortable. The sequence feels eerily familiar because so many of us have heard the details repeated for decades.

In a recent development, the preview then moves into the investigation and the attention that followed. Officers question what happened inside the home, reporters crowd the family, and suspicion increasingly falls on the parents. McCarthy's Patsy breaks down, insisting, "I didn't kill my baby." There's also a chilling moment when the district attorney, played by Shea Whigham, acknowledges that even the facts investigators can establish may never satisfy a public desperate for an explanation. It's a trailer built around grief and accusation, with no resolution waiting at the end.

According to recent reports, I think a lot of that comes down to remembering that JonBenét Ramsey was just 6 years old when she was murdered in 1996. Nearly 30 years later, her killing remains unsolved; nobody has been convicted, and her mother died in 2006 without ever seeing someone brought to justice for her daughter's death. In the decades since, JonBenét's murder has become the subject of countless documentaries, television specials, and endless speculation. Netflix itself released another docuseries about the case in 2024.

I understand that this fresh production may be trying to examine the media circus surrounding her death, and perhaps it will handle that responsibly. But watching the trailer, I couldn't stop thinking about how much entertainment we've already made out of this little girl's murder, and yet none seem to bring us any closer to understanding what happened.

The people making this series seem aware of that problem. McCarthy has spoken about how the public fascination with the mystery overshadowed the fact that parents lost their child, and Netflix claims the drama examines the consequences of the media frenzy. I appreciate that intention. Richard LaGravenese, the showrunner, is telling a story that cannot provide the ending audiences have spent years demanding. Boulder police still describe JonBenét's murder as an active investigation.

In a recent development, maybe the full series will find a thoughtful way to reckon with all of that. I'm certainly not questioning McCarthy's performance based on the footage we've seen. I just keep thinking about the difference between watching a fictional horror story and revisiting a real child's death and how much more uneasy the latter makes me. The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey premieres on Netflix Dec. 10 for everyone with a Netflix subscription. I'm not sure yet whether I'll be able to watch it.

Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (485 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game launched, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site.
  • Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB.
  • "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game launched, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This upcoming leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

Sources indicate that what does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

Industry observers note that cyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a upcoming version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO series, except that it's set during World War 2.
  • Originally developed by Random Games and published by Strategic Simulations, Inc, the game consists of 18 main scenarios spanning D-Day, Monte Cassino and Cherbourg.

It has been revealed that prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a upcoming version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO series, except that it's set during World War 2. I don't believe they had Chryssalids back then. Pretty sure grandpa never mentioned any Chryssalids.

Originally developed by Random Games and published by Strategic Simulations, Inc, the game consists of 18 main scenarios spanning D-Day, Monte Cassino and Cherbourg. There's a mission editor, too, and some standalone extra skirmishes. In each scrap, you pick eight men to undertake such feats as raiding V2 sites and hijacking disabled tanks, drawing on a dizzying range of individual soldier actions. Your squaddies level up with experience, and you can equip them with flamethrowers and bazookas. Among the key differences from X-COM is that there's no morale system - your men will never defy orders. Nor is there an overarching base/Geoscape layer.

Sources indicate that "This edition updates Soldiers at War to run smoothly on modern Windows systems, delivering improved compatibility and performance," promises the GOG page (it's also on Steam). "The game now supports 1280x720 widescreen resolution, with rendering improvements for smoother drawing." There are cloud saves and Achievements, too, for today's soldier is not content with merely laying down their life for their country. They must also unlock some percentage-based virtual trophies in the process.

Sources indicate that I remember Strategic Simulations, Inc mostly for working on two games in the Close Combat series, but they developed and published a shedload of other strategy games and wargames before their eventual parent company Ubisoft retired the brand in the noughties. As for Random Games – hold the phone, those guys also made the original Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate!

Sony’s struggling to meet demand for the PS5 following last week’s release of GTA 6.

Many major retailers in the US, including PS Direct, are at the moment completely sold out of the system – although you may find isolated instances of stock in stores.

Sources indicate that the platform holder has no promotions on hardware this Black Friday, presumably because it can’t meet demand at full-price. Remember, the console is significantly more expensive than it was at launch right now, due to spiralling global memory costs.

Writing on Bluesky, Circana analyst Mat Piscatella stated that PS5 hardware purchases increased 2.4x year-over-year in America through the week ending 14th November, just prior to the release of Rockstar’s open world.

Sony claims GTA 6 is the biggest launch in its history, and it observed “the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day since the console’s launch, outside of end-of-year holidays” on 19th November.

It added that for 70% of those newly connected consoles, GTA 6 was the first game played.

I imagine Sony is trying to get as many systems onto store shelves as it possibly can to meet this unprecedented demand, and I suspect demand will remain high through the holidays now.

In response to the situation, GameStop recently raised the price of used PS5 Pro consoles way beyond their already-sizeable MSRP.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.
  • Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet remarked mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet remarked mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

"Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises.".

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever.".

In a recent development, ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which rolled out last year.

Industry observers note that ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the company is run, with the publisher saying its new operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

According to recent reports, all leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Sources indicate that outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft says the newly introduced structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active users over the half.

That said, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

The news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft unveiled in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Sources indicate that since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that referring to the alleged executable as "an early Christmas gift", Cyberleek declared in the statement posted to their website that "the torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 leaker or leakers Cyberleek claim to to have released the main executable file for an alleged Xbox build of the game that they asserted they'd lobbed onto the net last week. In a fresh statement, the leakers alluded to the excutable being used in attempts to create an unofficial PC port of the crimsim, and denied that their use of cryptocurrency is just a grift.

Industry observers note that referring to the alleged executable as "an early Christmas gift", Cyberleek declared in the statement posted to their website that "the torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects". As of writing, the legitimacy of the executable doesn't appear to have been independently verified, meaning it could still just turn out to be a pile of malware or something similarly dodgy. Needless to say, given that and the fact software piracy is illegal, not touching it - or any of the other files Cyberleek claim to have posted - with a barge pole is the sensible thing to do.

Cyberleek have been bigging up the idea that these files they've been releasing could result in GTA 6 running on PC sharpish, via a modified version cobbled together with generative AI. That might happen, but I'm seriously skeptical that if it were to, it wouldn't just be dodgy jankware than runs like piss, rather than anything that'd compare remotely well to an official PC port.

Thus far, it appears a group of would-be recompilers going by Project Leonida may have got the game to start booting on PC, but they since look to have disappeared and scrubbed their established online presence.

All of this again raises the question of whether the threat of any sort of bodged PC recreation coming out of this alleged executable release may lead Rockstar to narrow the gap between this month's console release and its eventual Windows release, which reports have previously claimed is planned for the opening months of next year.

According to recent reports, returning to Cyberleek's latest statement, the leaker or leakers have also taken the opportunity to insist that their attempts to pump up a crypto coin as part of the leaking is just for practical reasons rather than grifty ones, honest. "Every donation is a vote for more of this," they wrote. "Where the votes go, [Cyberleek] follows. Crypto here is just a tool - there is no other way to move funds without names.".

Rockstar called the initial barrage of leaks laid claim to by Cyberleek "heartbreaking". Along with parent manufacturer Take-Two, they began a hunt for the identity of the leakers back in August, but that doesn't seem to to have deterred Cyberleek, if indeed the people leaking under the name are still the same ones as in the summer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As vibe coders desperately hurl commands at AI in an attempt to get GTA 6 running on PC, one former Destiny 2 dev claims it's led to the "most ridiculous dumpster fire ever" – one that, like a car crash, is hard to look away from.

Since notorious GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek dropped an Xbox build of the game last week – and more recently followed up with its executable file – multiple groups have been racing to get Rockstar's latest blockbuster up and running on PC. After all, it only rolled out on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, so there's a gap there for people without a console that folks have been desperate to fill – though I can't help but think that some hoping for their success might just be keen for a way to play GTA 6 for free.

In a recent development, anyway, it was always inevitable that people would try this, but the way they've been going about it has been messy, to say the least. We've already observed vibe coders begging their AI models of choice to do the GTA 6 port for them, "make no mistakes," and do it "faster," and former gameplay capture artist at Bungie, Amy Hendricks, has also been watching on in dumbfounded awe, documenting what she calls "the most ridiculous dumpster fire ever" in a thread on Bluesky.

She first looks at "the slopfest" she calls Project Leonida – one of the frontrunning decompilation projects that yesterday saw its Discord server completely disappear after Rockstar apparently got in touch, and its 15-year-old lead quit (though they've since told followers to "ignore" those posts, so who knows what's going on there). Before that, Hendricks documented: "One group feels like the chatbot developers are not moving fast enough (One reason being the main dev is still at school), so they're going to split the main GTA 6 recomp team into two via forking.".

It has been revealed that not long after that, fears began that Rockstar and Take-Two were on the way. A screenshot Hendricks shares from the Discord server before its apparent takedown reveals customers copy and pasting the same message they seemingly hoped would clear their name should any official investigation come about.

"In case of an investigation by any federal entity or similar, I do not have any involvement with this group or with the people in it, I do not know how I am here, probably added by a thrid party, I do not support any actions by the member of this group," they declare in unison. Yes, they all copied the same typos, too.

Despite all this, though, the vibe coders pressed on. An amusing highlight reveals one asking the AI why its task was taking so long, to be patiently told by the robot, "Each rebuild takes a long time, and the hang fix changes the shaders too, so it would need another rebuild.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Hendricks speculates that all these attempts are costing those involved some serious cash, too: "Fun fact: This is most likely using API Billing (Subs give you a small quota, API billing lets you go as far as your wallet allows), so everyone involved has most likely spent hundreds if not thousands of dollars already.".

Recent findings suggest that A follow-up post further explains that one of the people streaming their vibe coding efforts was using Fable 5.2, and "API pricing is built around the price of 1 Million tokens. Fable charges $8 for input (what it does) and $40 output (what it puts out) per 1M. If he's been doing this day and night for hours, easily thousands of dollars.".

It has been revealed that oh dear. Needless to say, it's not looking like a smooth operation. As Hendricks puts it, "I have always wanted to see the supposed 'expert programmers with AI making recomps' in action and it turns out it's just a bunch of kids hitting their head on a wall so im gonna keep watching out of morbid [curiosity].".

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Clever Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found a glitch with the Xbox version of the game that allows players to forcibly remove Rockstar's 30 fps cap.
  • Recent findings suggest that the glitch is surprisingly simple to perform: You just need to set the console's output to 60 Hz, load GTA 6, swap the output to 120 Hz, load a different game, and then use the Quick Resume feature to go back to GTA 6.
  • Industry observers note that in Digital Foundry's testing, GTA 6 doesn't suddenly become a buttery smooth 60 fps dream.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clever Grand Theft Auto 6 players have found a glitch with the Xbox version of the game that allows players to forcibly remove Rockstar's 30 fps cap. But even though people claim the game jumps up to 60 fps, the actual performance is nowhere near as smooth, according to Digital Foundry's tests.

Recent findings suggest that the glitch is surprisingly simple to perform: You just need to set the console's output to 60 Hz, load GTA 6, swap the output to 120 Hz, load a different game, and then use the Quick Resume feature to go back to GTA 6. For whatever reason, this forces the game to run above 30 fps, but not by much.

Industry observers note that in Digital Foundry's testing, GTA 6 doesn't suddenly become a buttery smooth 60 fps dream. Instead, it has an average frame rate of about 36 fps and still drops below that number during particularly intense scenes, like in city areas or when multiple cars are exploding due to rocket launcher hijinks.

It has been revealed that the most notable improvement is lower input lag when it manages to climb up to around 40 fps, but even that has an asterisk because the frame rate varies too much for the benefits to be consistent. Unless you strategy on spending your time in Leonida roleplaying as a fisherman, you're going to have a bad time.

While Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said an official 60 fps mode for GTA 6 is too much for the current generation of consoles to handle, including the PS5 Pro, Digital Foundry theorizes that a 40 fps mode might be possible in the future.

Recent findings suggest that I'm hopeful for console players, but none of this has stopped me from wanting the game on the only platform where 60 fps won't be much of a challenge to hit: PC. Tweaking settings you don't care as much about to juice the frame rate is much preferable over having to deal with a set "performance" mode or a glitch that could be patched out any day. A good PC version should be able to nicely scale up or down in performance based on your hardware setup, and Rockstar has shown that it can pull that off in the past with games like Red Dead Redemption 2.

For a game as good as GTA 6—Chris indicates it's "(mostly) great" in his 100-hour impressions— you shouldn't have to deal with quirks that tarnish the experience. I'm not a Rockstar employee, I don't know what challenges a PC version introduces or why it wasn't prioritized for a simultaneous PC and console release, but I do know that a PC version likely won't have as many caveats when it comes to performance as it does on consoles. So, I'll deal with Rockstar's intended 30 fps cap until the moment I can boot up GTA 6 on my PC, and then forget that I ever had to endure the limits of the current console experience.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.
  • Sources indicate that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast.
  • "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

Sources indicate that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

"I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon stated. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different.".

Sources indicate that he gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list.".

It has been revealed that moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

Recent findings suggest that it's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

According to recent reports, best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm presently ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

The Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

In a recent development, world of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arcade Archives 2 Dirt Dash will launch for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and Switch 2, and Arcade Archives Dirt Dash for PlayStation 4 and Switch, on November 26, developer Hamster confirmed. The Arcade Archives 2 version will cost $16.99 / 1,800 yen, while Arcade Archives version will cost $14.99 / 1,500 yen. An upgrade from Arcade Archives to Arcade Archives 2 will be available for $2.99 / 330 yen.

Here is an overview of the game, via Hamster:.

Dirt Dash is a racing game released by Namco Limited (current Bandai Namco Entertainment Inc.) in 1995.

Enjoy off-road racing through diverse environments, such as a SNOW stage heading down ski slopes, a Mountain stage running along mountain roads with steep cliffs, and a City stage navigating through urban alleyways.

Make full use of the course navigation system for route information, expertly clear the various action events along the way, and aim for the finish line!

The Arcade Archives series is developed with the concept of faithfully reproducing classic arcade games. It also includes convenient features such as difficulty and screen settings, rewind, rapid-fire, and multiple save slots. In addition, players can compete for the best scores with players around the world through online rankings.

Arcade Archives 2 series introduces a brand-latest mode called Time Attack Mode, in addition to the Original Mode, Hi Score Mode, and Caravan Mode from Arcade Archives. Time Attack Mode focuses on how quickly you can complete the game, regardless of the score you achieve.

What’s more, with VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) support, the gameplay can be reproduced even more accurately, closer to the original arcade experience.

Please enjoy these iconic arcade games that defined an era with the Arcade Archives series!

Spoilers ahead for Sunrise on the Reaping.

In a recent development, the Hunger Games movies (which are streaming with a Hulu subscription) have been wildly popular for a decade, and fans were recently treated to another book to screen adaptation with Sunrise on the Reaping. Francis Lawerence's new blockbuster featured younger versions of a number of beloved characters, with Stranger Things star Maya Hawke playing District 3 Victor Wiress. I wanted to see more of her towards the end of the movie, but the 28 year-old actress has another POV.

In a recent development, sunrise on the Reaping is crushing at the box office, showing how much the public still loved being in Panem. After Haymitch wins his games, we see a shot of Wiress looking bruised after being tortured by The Capitol about Beetee's proposal to break The Arena. I had the privilege of interviewing the cast ahead of the movie's release, where I asked Hawke if any scenes of her character ended up on the cutting room floor. She told me:.

No, I remember talking to Francis about this actually, and it would be too, too disturbing. You know, I think that with these movies, there's always a line that you're trying to walk of like telling the story as written and also making sure that it is like right for audiences. And I think that Francis remarked it would be too disturbing. And so we don't get to see really what happens, what goes down with us.

Recent findings suggest that despite being a franchise about young people killing each other, The Hunger Games movies have all been PG-13. As such, Lawrence and organization have to be specific about how violent the imagery can be. While I wanted to see more of Wiress, Hawke maintains that it would have been too "disturbing" to watch the beloved Victor being tortured by President Snow's forces. She's probably not wrong, as much as I wanted to see more of her take on the character.

A post shared by CinemaBlend (@cinemablend).

It has been revealed that later in our same conversation, Maya Hawke explained the upside of not having to shoot these difficult scenes as Wiress. As she told me:.

I'm grateful for it because those scenes are hard to act. By hard I mean like painful. Um, but I also was sad about it because they're fun and as well, so.

Obviously Hawke would have crushed it if we saw Wiress' torture and interrogation, but that ultimately wasn't something that was ever going to be part of Sunrise on the Reaping. The movie had to cut plenty of scenes like Maysilee killing a Gamemaker, although that wasn't the case for Hawke's character.

In our chat I asked the Do Revenge actress if Wiress had a mental break as a result of her torture, transforming her into the character we were introduced to by Amanda Plummer in Catching Fire. She confirmed to me:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It has been revealed that that's what Francis and I talked about, yeah. That's sort of like a substantial break that leads to the kind of version of her that we meet later.

I've still got FOMO about not getting more of Wiress, but I understand why it didn't happen. After all, Sunrise on the Reaping is a story about Haymitch above all. There was a ton of content to stuff into the movie's 158-minute runtime, so there was only so much time to dedicate to characters like Wiress and Mags.

According to recent reports, the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list. We'll just have to wait and see if Suzanne Collins gives us more prequel novels, allowing the beloved franchise to return to the big screen in the process.

Following the full game list for Awesome Games Done Quick being released a little while ago, GDQ have now published the full schedule for the event running for a week from January 3rd through January 10th in Atlanta (and streamed on Twitch, of course). Included amongst the latest games this year are 2026 releases like Queen's Domain, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, the Ocarina of Time remake, and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, which all make a lot of sense as games practically made for speedrunning. Belmont's Curse, specifically, is set to be the event's final bonus game, only to be played if donation incentives are met (which I'm sure they will be, it's a Castlevania game at GDQ).

But then, there's also Big Walk, which I'm fascinated by the prospect of trying to speedrun as a group. It's listed as a '12 player showcase', which I can only imagine denotes it as more of a fun experiment to put on a show, rather than a world-record aiming speedrun. The chaos of twelve people trying to work together in Big Walk live on the GDQ stage is a spectacle that has my interest, either way. Also making the cut is train-flipping stunt game Denshattack!, which I simply have to mention got a resounding "✨🚂DENSHATTACK MENTIONED🚂✨" from James in the RPS chat this morning. I can't help but share his excitement, in fairness, since Denshattack! is just that cool.

It has been revealed that as for some of the more out-there picks, which I say entirely positively, there's a run of not the DmC reboot, but specifically its bonus Vergil DLC, which is the first time I've heard that mentioned in years. Metroid Prime Origins, a fangame that 'demakes' the famously first-person Metroid Prime into a 2D sidescroller more akin to Zero Mission, is also on the cards; lovely to think there'll be a newly introduced speedrun for a new Metroid game just a month before Ravenous comes out. And finally, on a personal note because of my own biases, I'm deeply interested to see the Any% run of Yakuza 5 play out; that game is infamous for its ridiculous scope and length, so watching a runner try to get it down to only its most essential parts should be a treat. The schedule estimates around 2 hours for the run, to which I can only say good luck.

10 Books Like ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ You Should Read Next

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1282 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth.
  • The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.
  • An isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth. (Did I mention he's accompanied by his ex-girlfriend’s suddenly talkative cat?).

The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.

An isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone). He has magic that works like a video game, and has to deal with quests that slowly give him clothes (it’s a relief when he finally acquires some pants), force him to survive cannibals, and hunt down various monsters that definitely need killing. It’s got the same “gaming rules” structure as DCC and a similarly absurdist tone, with just the right spice of darkness.

It has been revealed that the Cradle series by Will Wight isn’t a LitRPG, and it doesn’t have Carl’s focus on humor, but it’s another progression fantasy with enough game-like elements to be a great match. Lindon is an “unsouled,” incapable of gaining any of the sacred arts and doomed to a life without a future. His lack of power makes Lindon ferociously determined to find an alternative path to power and success, and that’s what drives this story. He has to find creative ways to move forward, and slowly this leads him to a path that just might make him the most powerful person in his world. DCC fans will love the progression and the tone.

One of the key elements of any video game is the respawn—you get killed, but you pop back up to try again, sometimes at the beginning, sometimes at a save point. Django Wexler leverages that mechanic to great effect in How to Become the Dark Lord and Die Trying. Davi has been summoned to a fantasy world to be the hero, the person who defeats the Dark Lord and saves the day—but she’s failed (and died) so many times, she’s fed up, and decides that on this run through, she’s going to switch sides and become the Dark Lord, using all her knowledge gained from endless replays to her advantage. The humor is pitch-black the way DCC fans like it, and the progressive structure is a perfect fit.

Recent findings suggest that is Princess Donut your favorite part of Dungeon Crawler Carl? Of course she is. In that case, check out Andrew Seiple’s Threadbare series. Threadbare is a stuffed bear brought to magical life in a failed experiment. He’s a foot tall, full of stuffing, and extremely dumb when the story begins. But when he’s rescued by a little girl and plunged into a horrible series of dangers, Threadbare has to find a way to level up. Like DCC, Threadbare starts off leaning into the absurdity and humor, then slowly gains emotional gravitas as the story progresses.

It has been revealed that if you play tabletop RPGs, you’ve encountered a Murderhobo or two: A character who solves all their problems by killing—even members of their own party. Luke doesn’t aspire to be a Murderhobo—he just wants to take over the family business and hang with his buddies. But when an invasion threatens the kingdom, everyone over the age of 17 is ordered to be tested for Potential. Luke’s friends all test high and join the Ascender Corps, traveling to different planes for training. Luke tests ... very low, and when he steps through a portal to engage in his training, he finds himself without any guidance or training in a strange, deadly world where his only chance of survival is to murder his way through it. It’s dark, darkly funny, and a progression fantasy like no other.

According to recent reports, if you’re looking for a book series that combines the dark, chaotic humor, absurd game mechanics, and surprising emotional depth of Carl, here’s Ryan “Quicksave” Romano, a man who has the unique ability to literally create a save point in his existence that allows him to go back and redo things whenever he dies. Searching for a childhood friend, he becomes embroiled in a violent gang war that lets him make good use of his power—but underneath the snark and the insanity of Ryan’s existence is a surprisingly affecting story of a man who has suffered, and suffered countless tragedies that are definitely taking their toll.

If your fave bit of DCC is Carl himself—a mediocre dude in an extraordinary situation—you should read Dennis E. Taylor’s fantastic Bobiverse books. Bob is a software engineer who hits it big and promptly dies, waking up to discover a century has passed and he’s been repurposed as an AI controlling a space probe searching for new planets for humanity to inhabit. If he fails in his mission (and he’s not the only probe out there), he’ll be turned off for good. Luckily, he can make copies of himself, and he’s pretty smart. The humor here is smart and soaked in pop culture, making it a perfect match for DCC fans.

Want more of Carl’s absurdist humor? Mayor of Noobtown is the LitRPG you’re looking for. Jim dies and wakes up in a video game-esque universe and finds himself stuck in the zone designated for newbies—players with no experience, skill, or hope. The area fell out of the mainline progression mechanic a long time ago, so there doesn’t seem to be a way to gain power, and the monsters are not at all concerned about the unfairness of it all, so Jim has to figure out how to advance in a universe that seems designed to kill him (again).

According to recent reports, if you want to lean into the meta side of things, check out Scathing Reviewer, written by an author who goes by the unusual pen name "BananaDragon." Liu Peijin is the author of a sprawling LitRPG web novel, and she’s used to the bad reviews and complaints from readers—and quite combative about it. When her books’ universe blossoms into a very dangerous fresh reality, she should be perfectly positioned to survive, having written the story in the first place. But her story becoming real also means her insufferable protagonist is real, and all those nasty critics are now passing judgment on her entire existence. It’s a dark, funny takedown of the entire genre itself, and DCC fans will love it.

It has been revealed that if you want a story that parallels the dungeon crawling aspect of DCC, Andrew Rowe’s Arcane Ascension series is the ticket. The Serpent Spire is a tower of constantly changing traps, puzzles, and dangerous creatures. If you enter and survive, you emerge with magical powers. Corin Cadence’s brother entered the Serpent Spire years ago and never returned—and now Corin is determined not only to survive, but to make it to the top, where legend states a goddess will grant you whatever you wish. And what Corin wants is his brother back. It’s a literal progression combined with LitRPG rules, game-inspired puzzle-solving, and a complex magic system that fans of Carl will definitely enjoy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting.

The estimates come from data-tracking tech giant Sensor Tower (spotted by VGC), which has been watching GTA 6 pre-orders closely for weeks, updating estimates daily based on (unspecified) data that it collects.

In a recent development, should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6.

So far, Rockstar has said nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent firm Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. The question is "by how much?".

It has been revealed that reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In conversation with Automaton last month, the game's director Xiangyu Luo stated that "The game's content is already completely finished, and we're now at the stage of polishing its overall quality." As such, it would seem that this delay is to give the game a little more breathing room for bug fixes and quality assurance work, rather than rushing a holiday release just to hit its stated release window.
  • Based on my own time with Showa American Story, taking a little more time to clean it up would be a welcome choice.

Despite being announced back in 2022 with an initial release window of 2025, NEKCOM's action RPG Showa American Story has been set for a late 2026 release date for a while now. That seems to have changed, however, as the release date on its Steam page has slipped to 2027 without any sort of announcement as to why.

In conversation with Automaton last month, the game's director Xiangyu Luo stated that "The game's content is already completely finished, and we're now at the stage of polishing its overall quality." As such, it would seem that this delay is to give the game a little more breathing room for bug fixes and quality assurance work, rather than rushing a holiday release just to hit its stated release window.

Based on my own time with Showa American Story, taking a little more time to clean it up would be a welcome choice. When I played a demo at Gamescom 2026, I was a little stunned by how awful it felt to play. The protagonist was a blank slate designed to be pretty and nothing more, and the combat was mind-numbingly oversimplified, its challenge mainly derived from the need to wrestle with its janky controls and the noticeable delay between button presses and attacks. In that same interview, Luo notes an awareness of the game being compared to the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series in being a 'wacky' open-world action RPG, saying that he's "happy that players are making that association", as "it means they've recognised Showa American Story as a rich RPG with plenty of content to sink their teeth into." I can respect him taking the comparison in stride, but what I played seemed like a pale imitation of LAD that missed what makes that series more than it seems on the surface.

I can hope that this delay can result in improvements to the critiques the game has faced — Luo did mention that "we've heard many valuable comments regarding the feel of the controls and how the action is presented" — and that Showa American Story releases in a good state sometime in 2027.

Sources indicate that team Ninja's sequel received super strong reviews and it was fairly popular at launch, but it's fallen off a cliff in terms of recognition. That's largely because it launched so early on the 6th February, which has meant that it's been buried over the course of 2026.

In particular, the success of other, much more recent action games like Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Phantom Blade Zero has prevented it from even being brought up in most conversations.

Case in point: Nioh 3 hasn't received a single nomination at The Game Awards. It's nowhere to be seen under Best Action Game, Best Action / Adventure Game, or Best RPG.

Just anecdotally, I've seen a handful of Push Square users expressing their love for Nioh 3 in various comments sections; it's clearly got fans, but it feels like the game needs a miracle if it's to show up in any end-of-year discussions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has been shattering records since before it came out, becoming the top-rated game in the history of Metacritic before it had the biggest entertainment launch (by dollars) in history.
  • "More than 39 million unique players have experienced Jason and Lucia's story in Grand Theft Auto 6 on PlayStation 5," Sony content communications manager Tim Turi wrote in a blog post today.
  • But that's not a sales record—Rockstar still has a ways to go to surpass GTA 5's 230 million lifetime sales.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has been shattering records since before it came out, becoming the top-rated game in the history of Metacritic before it had the biggest entertainment launch (by dollars) in history. Sony is now joining in that victory lap by sharing GTA 6 milestones as they pertain to PlayStation.

"More than 39 million unique players have experienced Jason and Lucia's story in Grand Theft Auto 6 on PlayStation 5," Sony content communications manager Tim Turi wrote in a blog post today. That is a staggering number, especially considering GTA 6 also launched on Xbox and will (eventually) hit PC.

But that's not a sales record—Rockstar still has a ways to go to surpass GTA 5's 230 million lifetime sales. What is unprecedented, at least for PlayStation, is GTA 6's concurrents over launch weekend.

"GTA 6 set a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles," Turi said.

It has been revealed that that's the wild one to me, because that means more people were playing GTA 6 at the same time on the largest console platform than Call of Duty, GTA 5, or even Fortnite has ever achieved. Turi didn't share the concurrent figure itself, which is too bad—Steam remains the only platform that hands out exact player data. If the figure is theoretically higher than some of the biggest concurrent peaks we know about on Steam, then it could've been as high as 3-4 million players.

On average, those 39 million PS5 players logged 17.4 hours over four days. Let's just say my hour count represents the higher end of that average, and I'm still less than halfway through the main story.

Industry observers note that for a brief moment, Sauron ruled above all in The Rings of Power season 3, even likening his power to 'The One'. No, not the One Ring, but an even higher power – Eru Iluvatar, Middle-earth's answer to God.

While J.R.R. Tolkien largely kept The One away from the machinations of Middle-earth in his works (free will still exists in this fantasy world), Eru Iluvatar is a fascinating figure that bears further examination. The deity will also likely factor into The Rings of Power season 4, so it's time to get a headstart on who exactly He is.

Some spoilers for The Rings of Power season 3 ending follow.

Eru Iluvatar – also known as The One – is the creator of the world of Arda and its continents, including Middle-earth.

While he manifested the literal space of Middle-earth, The One left it up to angelic beings known as the Ainur and Valar (themselves created by Eru) to sculpt the land and create life within it.

In a recent development, eru Iluvatar rarely intervenes in matters in the world below, with the leader of the Ainur, Manwe, designated to – in effect – be his eyes and ears. Tolkien wrote of the godlike figure: "He was appointed to be, in the fullness of time, the first of all Kings: lord of the realm of Arda and ruler of all that dwell therein.".

According to recent reports, digging deeper into Tolkien's works reveals that Eru Iluvatar was planning to take mortal form in Middle-earth's Seventh Age. With Middle-earth actually being our planet, Tolkien lined up the years so Eru could feasibly be Jesus Christ. That idea only surfaced in a handful of correspondence, however, and never made it into the full literature. Even then, it's only an in-universe belief held by some religious observers.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

It has been revealed that as of The Rings of Power, Iluvatar is still worshipped as the one true God – especially in Numenor. Which makes Sauron's declaration that his power will make him stand above The One the worst possible sacrilege imaginable. So, will he descend from the heavens to ensure something is done? Well, about that….

Unless it deviates heavily from the source material, Eru Iluvatar will never show up – in a literal sense, anyway.

Spoilers for The Rings of Power season 4 follow, but with Sauron surrendering to Al-Pharazon, the Prime Video series is now on the path laid down by Tolkien, one which sees Numenor's ruler believing his power to be absolute. We won't go into specific details here, but Iluvatar does intervene at one point in one of Middle-earth's most shocking moments.

It has been revealed that eru's proxies and servants have also appeared in The Rings of Power. The Secret Fire, the power used by Iluvatar to create the world, appeared before Gandalf in season 3 and bestowed upon him the quest to unite once more with Pallando to help stop Sauron.

The Great Eagles have also turned up on multiple occasions, and they are emissaries of Iluvatar's right-hand angel Manwe and show up at moments of great importance.

Dancing Dragons Games and Hooded Horse have unveiled Symphony of War II: Dominion, the sequel to 2022's Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga. Sin noted the original as pretty special for being "a good strategy game", highlighting the unique importance of taking care of each and every army member, rather than just benching the ones that are less effective and/or pretty to look at. The Nephilism Saga is also somewhat rare in being a turn-based tactics game made in RPG Maker, as seems to be the case with its sequel, which is expanding to include naval combat.

Symphony of War II: Dominion Announcement Trailer | Strategy RPG Watch on YouTube.

Dominion's premise mirrors its predecessor in setting a band of heroes from a wide variety of classes, with units ranging from heavy knights and light archers to cannon-lighting artillery and even dragons the size of large dogs; I do have to wonder if an actual hooded horse is one of the units. Over 100 different classes are available, with the core of the game being swapping out these units to create the most effective squads of units for each turn-based battle. As before, it's not just a matter of recruiting soldiers and never thinking about them again until their turn arrives; a cared for army is a strong army (Sun Tzu stated that, probably), and nurturing your army with new gear, individual perks and specialisation to make the squad work not only on their own, but as a collective.

Phil Hamilton, founder of Dancing Dragon Games, elaborated that "With Symphony of War: Dominion, we’re building on what players loved about the first game while taking the series in a direction we’ve wanted to explore for years. We’re delivering a deeper, more ambitious strategy RPG without sacrificing the feel and flow that made the original special." Symphony of War II: Dominion releases sometime next year, so for now, get thinking about how you'll best take care of your squads. To paraphrase Sun Tzu again, keeping them fed is always a good start.
