💡 Key Takeaways
  • There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000.
  • Recent findings suggest that in an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet.
  • Sources indicate that the star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

Recent findings suggest that in an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

Sources indicate that the star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do.".

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

As you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

On the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

According to recent reports, "Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that.".

According to recent reports, total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

  • He recalls an example of someone making an Android port of Graveyard Keeper, which "barely fit into memory", and was surprised by how "easy" it seemed.

GenAI game clones are apparently becoming a real enough threat to the industry that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick pre-warned "this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent," while threatening legal action against anyone who naughtily tinkered with GTA VI. More recently, one or more apparent crypto grifters claim to have naughtily tinkered with GTA VI, sparking attempts to vibe-recomp an unoffical PC version. However, contrasting Zelnick's position is tinyBuild CEO Alex Nichiporchik, who quite confidently stated in an interview with Gamesindustry.biz that "devs shouldn't be afraid of it.".

Nichiporchik discusses tinyBuild's approach to the gap between announcement and release being crucial in the age of slop copies (I am trying not to write 'sloppies' into my article, but it is tempting), explaining that "The traditional wisdom previously was to announce early, build up as many wishlists as possible over time, and then you'll have a good basis to launch your game eventually. And that seems to be changing fundamentally." He adds that maintaining a short gap also helps as, to put it simply, "people have short memories, right?" And, unfortunately, he's right; there are so many games coming out that adding something to your wishlist often feels like resigning it to remembering it exists six months later.

He recalls an example of someone making an Android port of Graveyard Keeper, which "barely fit into memory", and was surprised by how "easy" it seemed. But then, he clarifies that the reason it seemed so easy was a lack of care. "There's a reason that every kind of AI slop game feels the same; it's because when you try to make something from zero, AI will multiply your skills, and zero times a thousand is still zero." The people claiming to 'develop' recomps do not care for making a game that feels right, or even one that works; they care only for the short-lived dopamine of being popular on Twitter for fifteen minutes before another slop copy rears its head (and is inevitably revealed to be jankware). Nichiporchik specifies that "game feel is impossible to copy; as long as you have a great game feel and a great game loop, I think you're going to be okay." 'Game feel' is one of the vaguest terms that exists in this field, but I do feel that it refers to something tangible and immediately noticeable when it's gone.

It has been revealed that for example, I've recently been replaying the wonderful Celeste, and the 'game feel' of its wavedashing is core to making the practice of blazing through levels so engaging. The wavedash works the same every time, due to precise programming from Extremely OK Games spending time and effort painstakingly ensuring it did in the interest of consistency and unity in movement mechanics. You can't make good art without caring about the quality, even if there are now faster ways to knock together a 'working' game. To borrow an overused but still salient phrase: AI could never.

Grand Theft Auto 6's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full".

In a recent development, "Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it.".

Downing Street went on to address the issue of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters".

The leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns. "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else.".

Sources indicate that GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

This state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Final Fantasy Resonance has been one of the most positively-received Square Enix games in ages — but its developers were never fully convinced that it would, er, resonate on the scale that it has.

Producer Keisuke Nakashima told Japanese outlet Game*Spark (as translated by Automaton): "I was surprised to see just how many people, not only in Japan but overseas as well, are eager for the kind of FF they remember from back in the day, with classic turn-based battles and pixel art.".

Of course, this quote feeds into a debate that's been raging amongst fans of Final Fantasy for over a couple of decades at this point.

There are many who believe that the series has long since lost its way, pushing to innovate with more and more action-focused gameplay instead of drawing from the turn-based and command battle systems that helped establish the franchise as a world-beater in the first place.

Titles like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 are constantly brought up as living proof that turn-based RPGs can still be blockbusters — but Square Enix has only veered further and further away from Final Fantasy's traditional blueprint with each mainline instalment.

Resonance may be a lower-budget spin-off, but at least to some extent, it does go against the publisher's line of thinking that Final Fantasy must appeal to a "wider audience" if it's to maintain its flagship status.

"We figured [Resonance] was something we ourselves would enjoy, and that there would be players out there who’d feel the same way," says Nakashima.

Director Hiroto Furuya adds: "I thought this was a rather unconventional title, so I expected opinions on it might be divided.".

He then references Resonance's foundations, having been built on the bones of now defunct mobile title Final Fantasy Brave Exvius: "I think the fact that a game with such an unusual background has been embraced by so many people is a positive for the industry as a whole, and I’m personally very happy to see it.".

Without wanting to be overly critical of games I really enjoy, like Final Fantasy 16, I do think Square Enix has been guilty of chasing a goal that simply may not exist.

This mythical "wider audience" has been the downfall of many games over the years, and you can argue that Final Fantasy has chipped away at its own identity and strength of brand in the (pretty desperate) pursuit of fresh fans.

Resonance isn't going to sell millions upon millions of copies, but the way it's been embraced says a lot about the current state of Final Fantasy as a whole, I feel.

And remember, recent reports strongly suggested that the suits at Square Enix wanted Resonance to be a basic port of the aforementioned mobile title, presumably in a bid to keep costs down.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in a recent interview with Korean outlet Inven, CD Projekt Red's narrative director Philipp Weber and vice president of story Marcin Blacha shared some words on The Witcher 4, focusing on their awareness that not only will it inevitably be different from The Witcher 3, but also that it needs to be in order to justify its existence. Simultaneously, there's a certain something to The Witcher as a series that they feel is difficult to make tangible, but is something they want to ensure they don't lose sight of.

Weber describes the core of a 'Witcher-like' story to be something that "explores the various facets of human nature — a game for adults", which he clarifies doesn't just mean violence or sex, but "treating the player as a mature adult, asking difficult questions without offering easy answers." While it has been quite a while since its predecessor, they still feel that the upcoming sequel must be true to the series it's part of and earn that numbered title: "If we were to strip away The Witcher's distinct edge just to reach a broader audience, it would end up appealing to no one.".

Of course, the biggest change is that of the protagonist, from Geralt to Ciri. Blacha explains that "Ciri isn't calm and composed like Geralt, nor does she hide her emotions easily. She is far more hot-headed and tends to be emotional when making decisions." In terms of how this actually affects the narrative itself and the protagonist's place in it, he elaborates that "when playing as Geralt, players acted more like an arbiter judging how to resolve a situation. When playing as Ciri, you are much more deeply involved in the story through her personal perspective." It's an interesting notion, to state that the difference in role is that where Geralt was more of a fixer, Ciri actually approaches situations on an interpersonal level. Weber seemingly half-jokes that "we find ourselves in a position very similar to Ciri's. Just as Ciri must succeed Geralt, we must create a game that lives up to The Witcher 3.".

As for how The Witcher 4 will play, moment to moment, Weber explains that some inspiration has been taken from Cyberpunk 2077 in regards to its open, player-led approach to customisation and, as a result, quests. "You could be a netrunner or a cyber ninja air-dashing into a scene with a double jump. We had to account for all those possibilities available to the player," he recalls. While I can't imagine Ciri will be air-dashing around Kovir, this statement does make me wonder how this approach can be applied to a game with such a specific existing protagonist, rather than the blank slate of Cyberpunk 2077's V. Recalling the side content of The Witcher 3 and its acclaim, he believes that people loved them "because we strived to offer something fresh" and "didn't create quests that merely waste the player's time", which is a principle that "remains unchanged today." Later, he condenses his feelings into the mantra that "A great quest can stem from a compelling story, an engaging character, or fantastic gameplay alone, but overall, there must be harmony.".

Towards the end of the interview, Blacha jokes that "One of our greatest achievements is convincing people to finish their workday, buy our game, and then clock into another job as a character inside the game." It's quite a long and engaging read, so if you're invested in The Witcher IV and its narrative development, I do encourage you read the entire thing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fuse Games, the developer of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, has mentioned it "didn't dream" the pod racing game's background character Biddy Blas would become as popular as he has.

Since Galactic Racer's release in October, Blas - who resembles a short, humanoid crocodile (officially a crocin) - has become a viral sensation. The combination of his unexpected swagger and ridiculous high-pitched Huttese monologues - performed irresistibly by actor Richard Summers-Calvert - have made him a fan favourite, especially his catchphrase "scrib doon" (which means "write it down").

It has been revealed that "Here's a name for you, amateur!" Blas tells the player upon meeting them, albeit in Huttese. "Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!".

Fuse Games shared a comment from Biddy Blas creator and Galactic Racer narrative designer Ren Alex-Rose about the character's success. "We always suspected Biddy Blas would be a popular member of the Galactic League, but we didn't dream of just how popular he'd become," Alex-Rose said.

"He was an incredibly enjoyable character to build, from our early ideation of a small, angry non-human character (who we lovingly referred to as our cast's 'chaos goblin') to recording his sometimes-absurdist dialogue with Blas' voice actor, who took the crocin to a whole new level.

It has been revealed that "It's been great watching Biddy Blas emerge into his assured self, as well as seeing the community embrace him for it. He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly.".

Sources indicate that blas' breakout success was praised by Lucasfilm producer Craig Derrick, who said his social feeds were filled with posts about Galactic Racer, though mostly about Biddy Blas. And the enthusiasm actor Richard Summers-Calvert was greeted with during October's MCM Comic-Con in London, which I attended, was palpable. There's a nice video of him doing Blas' voice on Instagram.

In a recent development, star Wars: Galactic Racer was awarded a full five stars in Eurogamer's review. "Both a surprisingly fun Roguelite campaign and a racing treat for Criterion fans, this is just wonderful stuff," wrote Christian Donlan.

Every GTA 6 fence location and where to find them

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are seven different GTA 6 fences you can find, with locations all over the map.
  • These are all the fences that are available in GTA 6.
  • Let's take a look now at these options in more details.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are seven different GTA 6 fences you can find, with locations all over the map. But which you’ll have access to depends on where you are in Jason and Lucia’s journey as you work though all the GTA 6 Missions. They all offer different rates for different goods, with two that are specific to cars, so it’s handy to keep track of what your options are and where you can find them.

These are all the fences that are available in GTA 6. However, they’re not all available at the same time and all offer different services:.

Let's take a look now at these options in more details.

Brian is Jason’s earliest contact in the criminal world, so it’s not surprising that he would be your first fence. But it’s a good thing that he becomes inaccessible after the end of Chapter 1, because his rates are as low as they go.

Another early game fence, leaving narcotics at Donnie’s trailer will get you a slightly better rate than going through Brian, while it’s the same rate for jewelry and marked bills. But Donnie becomes inaccessible even earlier than Brian, so if you have drugs to sell, make sure you drop them off in good time before the Swamped mission.

In Chapter 2, you’ll unlock the ability to fence stolen cars when you meet Moses. He also has a list he’s willing to pay more for. He won’t take anything with a tracker, though – you’ll have to wait until Chapter 3 before you’re able to sell these more advanced cars.

Dunk becomes an available fence after the aptly named Slam Dunk mission in Chapter 2. When that mission is complete, you’ll be able to find Dunk’s trailer near the centre of Port Gellhorn. He doesn’t pay very much, but he stays available as you progress through the game, so if you find yourself on the western side of the map and don’t want to bother driving over to Vice City, he’s still a viable option.

Once you make it to the major city in Chapter 3, you’ll be offered a mission called Tyrone, which will introduce you to one of the fences who will be useful for the rest of the game. Tyrone pays highly for narcotics, and also at a medium rate for jewelry and marked bills. Note that you might be better off going to Yasmani for those other two though – he’s not far away, as you can see below.

It has been revealed that found not too far away from Tyrone, and unlocked not too long afterwards, is Yasmani. He pays highly for jewelry and marked bills, so it’s best to split those off to him while taking any narcotics you’ve picked up over to Tyrone.

Industry observers note that finally in Chapter 3, you’ll unlock Randy, who can deal with all kinds of cars regardless of their trackers. Like Moses, he also has a list of desired vehicles, which can be turned into him for high payouts – but he’ll take anything you happen to lift, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a round of layoffs last month that resulted in the loss of 40 jobs, which itself came after a previous source of funding pulled out in the Spring, independent studio Gravity Well has now announced that it is going into "hibernation" for the foreseeable future. The team was largely made up of devs who'd left Titanfall and Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment, and under the Gravity Well banner had been working on a new, still-unannounced game for around six years.

A statement posted to the main page on Gravity Well's site reads:.

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building. Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we’re going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you’re a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.

If you’re a publisher or investor and are interested in talking, let's connect!".

Recent findings suggest that the message is signed off by its founders Drew McCoy, Jon 'Slothy' Shiring and Mon Saetern. Besides being the second project led by former Respawn developers to be doomed this year - see also Wildlight's Highguard - it's unfortunately another case of a studio made up of developers with incredible pedigrees being left at the whim of funding accruement in the current state of the industry. That said, it is noteworthy that the team have not shown anything publicly in the six years since their formation, minus a few pieces of concept art which can now be seen on its site. It's still unknown exactly what Gravity Well was working on, but it's likely to have been some kind of movement-based shooter, if the teams' experience on Titanfall, Apex Legends and Call of Duty is anything to go by. Solidarity to all affected, who I hope can find work elsewhere in the industry.

Although she recently claimed there's something she won't do with her relationships moving forward. Let's break it all down.

Sources indicate that recently Jennifer Lopez joked about her divorces, showing that the 57 year-old icon has a good sense of humor about it all. Still, it sounds like she's changing the way she approaches future relationships. In a conversation on the Fresh York Times podcast, she shared how she wants to keep her romantic life more private moving forward. In the "Let's Get Loud" singer's words:.

It has been revealed that I’m guarded in the sense that I want to protect my loved ones, and I want things to be more sacred in my life. And I’ve learned lessons about being out there with relationships and stuff. That’s not something I ever want to do again.

Honestly, this makes a great deal of sense. Fans have been obsessed with JLo's love life for years now, making her personal life into a very public matter. Before her divorce from Affleck was finalized there were rumors about them being separated for months. Sources indicate that while in the podcast, the Selena actress spoke about what she's learned from her very public celebrity relationships. She went on to say:.

That’s not something I ever want to do again, as far as sharing that part of my life with people. It’s not that people won’t know. They’ll see me in the street, they’ll follow you. They’ll do this, and they’ll see you. But at the same time, it’s not something I want to comment on. It’s not something I’m inviting people into, it’s not something I’m putting on display. That’s not something I’m interested in anymore.

Honestly, I wouldn't blame her! She's made countless headlines and been photographed by paparazzi for decades now related to who she was dating and/or married to. Now that she's in a newly introduced stage in her life, some privacy might be exactly what Jennifer Lopez needs.

Fame is a double-edged sword, and JLo knows all too well how difficult it can be to have one's life under a microscope. She spoke more about the toll that it's taken over the years, saying:.

Sources indicate that I really feel this thing, that energy, whatever it is, this mechanism that exists this machine…. whatever we want to call that thing, is a destructive, hurtful machine, you know what I mean?

Perhaps it's because of this that we haven't gotten any official confirmation about Jennifer Lopez's rumored relationship with Brett Goldstein. Only time will tell if they're actually dating, but her comments might offer some context about why it's still firmly a rumor a this time.

In a recent development, another day, another Steam update! Earlier this year, Valve made some tweaks to Steam's Community Market as part of their ongoing widening of the digital storefront. The maybe Half-Life 3 developer is back with another update for the Community Market, once again bringing some fresh UI/UX bits, as well as some quality of life adjustments that should make it a bit nicer to use.

According to recent reports, for starters, there's a new Market home page! "We've rebuilt the Market Home to load faster and present you with the most relevant items from your games," a blog post explains. "Instead of the Popular Items section, which was a small and static slice of millions of items, Trending Items will give you a glimpse into what’s new in the games you’re currently playing. The game links move up to the top spot and are now personalized, so rather than a flat and unchanging list, you get quick access to the items you're most likely to be interested in.".

Industry observers note that next up in the enhancement is the addition of a watchlist feature. Before, if you wanted to follow a number of items in the marketplace you'd need to bookmark everything, but now you can just save things to your watchlist; this includes the likes of specific listings, particular item types with any filters you've applied, and even specific searches, again with filters and search text. You can also apply custom names to watchlist entries in case two of them end up looking particularly similar.

There were a few other smaller bits to this update too. You'll find a latest section that highlights Steam community items, i.e. trading cards and emotes, from games you've played. If you have anything listed on the marketplace, you can now change the price without having to relist it. There's a list view option while browsing items. And market pages now load faster and are more responsive. A convenient sounding update for the Steam Community Market connoisseur! Which is already live, by the way.

  • According to recent reports, the fresh market home is, says Valve, faster to load up, but it's not just a new gloss of paint.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you're normal, you probably never think about the Steam community market. If you're like me, you only touch it to sell the mountains of trading cards you get from idling. If you're a true lunatic, you're running a roaring trade in Counter-Strike 2 skins and are either unfathomably rich or trapped in a life of penury.

Either way, some news: Valve has been tinkering at the Steam marketplace again, and in an patch yesterday unveiled a rebuilt market home page that's slightly more pleasant to handle and look at, while being more personalised to the games you're actually playing. This is in addition to a set of changes to the market Valve released (in beta) back in May.

According to recent reports, the fresh market home is, says Valve, faster to load up, but it's not just a new gloss of paint. It's swapped out the pre-enhancement Popular Items section—which mostly just indicated a list of CS2 crates—for new Trending Items lists that show the popular market items for games you've actually been playing. When I look at it, I see Path of Exile, Warframe, Crisis In The Kremlin, and, uh, Dota 2. I've never touched Dota 2 in my life, so not sure what's happening there, but you get the idea.

You've also now got a watchlist that will let you keep track of various market items across multiple games. You can save specific items, a general item type, or even a particular search. I imagine this will be useful to those of you who play the Steam market like an '80s Wall Street guy shouting into a big phone.

The biggest change for me personally—that's why people read the news, for the biggest changes for me personally—is streamlined selling and relisting. You can now change the price of items you have listed for sale without laboriously taking them down and relisting them. You can just update the price tag and have done with it. Similarly, if you're selling directly from the Steam mobile app, you'll be able to approve those sales via a pop-up rather than navigating to the confirmation page. This is truly huge news for the weirdest guys you know (me).

All that aside, the market home page will now also track your in-progress badges, and search results now have a list view. There are a few more latest things, but Valve confined them to an 'and finally' set of bulletpoints, so here they are in their original bulletpoint form.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that chinese police have arrested 13 individuals in Shanghai allegedly involved in a bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine business, after consumers reported the operation. They are at the moment being investigated on suspicion of selling infringing reproductions.

Reported by Gamespark, the police cracked down on the operation which involved the seizure of around $300,000 of goods related to the figurines.

The investigation started in May, after police received reports from concerned members of the public about the Tifa figurines. They were made from different materials than official figurines, and after confirming the illegitimacy of these products with the rights holders, Square Enix, police determined these businesses were not authorised to be producing such goods and went to work.

The appearance of these counterfeits were deemed identical to the real merch, and therefore the alleged crime was deemed infringement of official goods. These counterfeits also came in different sizes, some of which were more expensive than the originals and customisabile.

According to recent reports, looking at pictures taken by local outlet Shangguan News (and put side-by-side by Automaton), you can see the official Tifa figurine (right) next to the counterfeit version (left). Both show Tifa in a blue dress, though the materials used are clearly different.

The third entry in the remake trilogy, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is coming in April 2027, and is looking good judging from early previews.

💡 Key Takeaways

Recent findings suggest that for publicly traded game developers, there is surely one question, with all manner of variations, that will surely be coming up again and again over the next few months: what impact will GTA 6 have on your games? CD Projekt Red were subjected to such questioning in their latest earnings call, part of which was related to sales figures of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, that boring kind of thing. But CEO Michal Nowakowski did also respond to a comment about how GTA 6 may affect the development of The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2.

"We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4 and] Cyberpunk 2, they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6," Nowakowski quite plainly explains in response to a question about how the biggest game of the year may influence budget or design, already sounding just that little bit exasperated over the questions related to Rockstar's latest. "If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done. That's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers. In terms of the budget, I gave a response [in an interview at] Gamescom; games The Witcher or Cyberpunk 2, although they are not GTA, are not budget-driven developments.".

Recent findings suggest that nowakowski goes on to clarify that he doesn't mean this in the sense of not caring about budgets, or that they have infinite money, but noted that you "cannot make games," with solely that focus. "They are ambition-driven developments and money is vital, the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6." This is obviously kind of a non-answer in one sense, but I think it does point to how GTA 6 is going to create some uncomfortable expectations for many triple-A devs when next to none of them will have Rockstar money to fulfill them.

Sources indicate that in any case, obviously the next major thing for CD Projekt Red is The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion. Still no release date attached to that one, though it's at the moment expected to release sometime in 2027 next year. The Witcher 4 is then slated for release not long after that in 2028, but in this day and age, I'm sure a delay would be an incredibly safe bet to make.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the bigger breakout success stories of the year is Wardogs. The military shooter's team-based approach to the battle royale template managed to bring in hundreds of thousands of players after going public back in September. Its success is in contrast to where Battlefield 6 is at right now, and one of the lead devs believes EA's series just isn't taking the right approach to stimulating the community.

"I don't think [Battlefield Studios] did anything different; I think they just dressed it up differently," Joe Brammer, co-founder and CEO of Wardogs studio Bulkhead, tells Hivemind World.

Recent findings suggest that "'Oh, we're going to run a massive campaign where we get everyone on Discord and we have the Battlefield Labs and you come and play test stuff,'" he notes. "If you're not actually going to change the game that much based on what people say, then it's not really.".

Sources indicate that how different Battlefield 6 is from previous entries and the impact of Battlefield Labs are both hard to definitively quantify, but the available stats don't paint a strong picture. The sixth mainline entry in the first-person shooter franchise started strong, but on PC at least, concurrent player numbers have settled into the 20,000-30,000 range.

Not bad, but not Earth-shaking either, and half of what Wardogs tends to do on Steam daily. Brammer points to the constant effort to follow the community's desires as part of Battlefield's downfall, because it contributed to a lack of overall direction.

"If you look at how we're doing things, we absolutely clarify all the time, like, 'No, no, we're not going to constantly take feedback and use it,'" he notes. "Sometimes we will; sometimes there's some good stuff. But like, there's often just not. I think they fell into that trap of doing whatever the community says and the players say.".

According to recent reports, this seems contentious because I've seen plenty of Battlefield players who feel they're never heard, while I imagine there are others who've had every complaint rectified. Managing huge releases like Battlefield 6 must be all-consuming at times, with no obvious game plan regardless of your goals.

Brammer adds that his team refers to Battlefield players as "homeless" internally because they tend to splinter off toward Wardogs, Escape from Tarkov, or something else entirely. Whatever they're up to, perhaps Battlefield 7 will be what unifies them once again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An investigation into the workplace behavior of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned recently after a series of extramarital affairs came to light, has uncovered decades of harassment, verbal employee abuse and "cultish" behaviour at the organization which has long played a major role in PC gaming.

In a recent development, following Huang's departure, The Fresh York Times has published a report in which "more than a dozen" current and former Nvidia employees discussed their experiences with the former CEO. Speaking on conditions of anonymity, employees alleged Jensen Huang would verbally berate them, reportedly going as far as to say he'd rip their arms off, rip their heart out and stomp on it, or rip their head off and "pee on your brain".

Recent findings suggest that the report includes numerous examples of Huang's alleged abusive behaviour, which apparently stretches back years before Nvidia became the one of the most valuable companies in the world - years before the AI boom. It's claimed Huang on one occasion went around a room of managers telling them he'd kill them. Then, when he reached a person in their 70s, mentioned everyone hoped they'd drop dead.

According to recent reports, huang allegedly referred to these bouts of public humiliation as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia, when questioned by an internal HR employee whom he later fired for not being a "right fit". Huan's stance was apparently to test whether a person could handle the culture there, which is described in the report as "cultish".

It's claimed Huang's influence at Nvidia has meant other senior managers have followed his lead, including his daughter Madison, Nvidia's chief of staff, who it's said often yells at staff, including executives more highly ranked than her.

Recent findings suggest that A spokesperson for Huang denied the allegations in response to a request for comment by the New York Times. The spokesperson, John Fisher, said the claims in the report were "fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false".

Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO earlier this month after a series of extramarital affairs were unearthed - one with a person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy, and two others with Nvidia employees. The chair of Nvidia's board, Harvey C. Jones, reportedly stated earlier this week that the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the sixth region to be added to the game, and the "penultimate challenge," implying that there's just one more area to come after this one, The Core takes you to Habitation Blue's reactor sector.
  • There are a few newly introduced subregions to be found too, of course, but more importantly a new major artifact.

In a recent development, the beauty of stepping into a digital world is that it allows me to accomplish things I couldn't possibly dream of doing in the real one, like, say, climbing anything that's higher than your average step ladder. White Knuckle is one such game that's all about playing around with uncomfortable heights, and a new update for the early access roguelike went live this week introducing a new, hostile environment: The Core.

Recent findings suggest that the sixth region to be added to the game, and the "penultimate challenge," implying that there's just one more area to come after this one, The Core takes you to Habitation Blue's reactor sector. "Use everything you have available to fight through the now Mass-controlled Superstructure Automated Processing System (SAPS) and her array of mechanized defenses," explains a Steam news post. "The Core is the sterile power station of the Superstructure, a massive network of coolant lines, offices, catwalks, and more, all of which is highly secured by an army of turrets, drones, and androids. Even without the Mass hot on your tail it would not be easy to escape.".

There are a few newly introduced subregions to be found too, of course, but more importantly a new major artifact. It's called The Scissors, and with it you cut off your hands ("yes, really") to "gain a spectral form that increases your reach, hand stamina, and damage," while using the artifact. You can also throw the scissors like a boomerang to hurt enemies from afar, and "killing enemies also counts as eating if using Survival Mode binding, or the perks Conditioned Polyphagia & Unstoppable Conviction.".

In a recent development, beyond this there's a selection of upcoming weapons, like the piton crossbow which shoots "pitons at range, to set up routes and to deal extreme damage." The pulse pump is a new trinket that introduces a chargeable mid-air jump. There's new perks like one called nest egg, where you gain a "second major artifact at the start of the Nest, at the cost of halving all roach deposits in your run." Previous regions have also received some new room tiles, and there's a few fresh cosmetics to pick up too. There's some secret thing to find in this update as well, "but you'll need to play to find out…" Hop to it, I guess!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Publisher Aniplex and developer French-Bread released the main trailer and latest information for fighting game Melty Blood: Twi-Lumina during a TYPE-MOON Times special news program today, revealing the key visual, playable character Satsuki Yumizuka, cross-play, Grand Scenario Mode, the “Act” and “Duel” control modes, and the early purchase bonus.
  • A Digital Deluxe Edition was also confirmed, which includes the base game and a digital art book.
  • In Japan, pre-orders for physical standard and limited editions for PlayStation 5 and Switch will begin on November 26.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Publisher Aniplex and developer French-Bread released the main trailer and latest information for fighting game Melty Blood: Twi-Lumina during a TYPE-MOON Times special news program today, revealing the key visual, playable character Satsuki Yumizuka, cross-play, Grand Scenario Mode, the “Act” and “Duel” control modes, and the early purchase bonus.

A Digital Deluxe Edition was also confirmed, which includes the base game and a digital art book.

In Japan, pre-orders for physical standard and limited editions for PlayStation 5 and Switch will begin on November 26. The latter includes a copy of the game, decorated box featuring artwork by Takashi Takeuchi, an art book, the original soundtrack, an arcade controller button-style tin case featuring artwork by Takeuchi, and a set of three 30-millimeter arcade controller style buttons (Len, White Len, and Satsuki Yumizuka), also by Takeuchi, with a strap.

Fresh Key Visual by Takashi Takeuchi Revealed!

Aniplex unveiled a newly drawn illustration by Takashi Takeuchi, who is handling the character designs for this title. In addition to the two characters, Shiki Tohno and Arcueid, the visual features Ren, White Ren, and Satsuki Yumizuka, who will make their debut as playable characters in the upcoming game.

Satsuki Yumizuka Makes Her Debut as a Fresh Playable Character.

The new trailer not only introduces the new character, and new game play systems added specifically in this title, but also the Grand Scenario Mode created by Kinoko Nasu.

The video also features the game’s theme song, Welcome To My Dream (feat. 310), produced by Spiral Ladder.

Upcoming Battle System and Cross-Platform Multiplayer.

Recent findings suggest that during the most recent stream of TYPE-MOON Times: Melty Blood: Twi-Lumina Latest Information Special, Ryosuke Kanemoto as Shiki Tohno and Yohei Azagami as Mikhail Roa Baldamyon were joined by development director Kamo Serizawa. Together they revealed the latest information on the game, including new game systems added in this title, which includes the series’ first cross-platform versus mode, as well as the Grand Scenario Mode created by Kinoko Nasu. The versus play also features the new playable characters Ren and White Ren.

First Cross-Platform Multiplayer Feature.

This title in the Melty Blood series is slated to be the first of its kind in supporting cross-platform play, which allows players to battle against more players across different platforms.

Recent findings suggest that the Act control scheme, which allows players to move the character with simple controls by activating special moves with the press of a single button. This is recommended for those latest to fighting games or the Melty Blood series.

Sources indicate that the Duel control scheme, which lets players enjoy more authentic battles by utilizing precise controls through traditional command inputs. This play style is recommended for those familiar with fighting games or players who want to delve deeper into the game mechanics.

Grand Scenario Mode includes newly introduced story by Kinoko Nasu.

The new Grand Scenario Mode is a large-scale scenario feature newly added to this title.

Players can enjoy a story written exclusively for this game by Kinoko Nasu that focuses on the protagonist, Shiki Tohno. The story is presented through a variety of narrative techniques, and more information is available on the official website, as well as during the TYPE-MOON Times: Melty Blood: Twi-Lumina Latest Information Special.

Round call voices for Ren, White Ren, and Satsuki Yumizuka will be added to the main game.

Melty Blood: Twi-Lumina is due out for PlayStation 5, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC via Steam on April 22, 2027.

Watch a new trailer and today’s TYPE-MOON Times program below. View a new set of screenshots at the gallery.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the comedian and talk show host was among the A-listers who scored an invite to the Tayvis wedding.
  • In a recent development, so my wife and I are watching Phoebe Waller-Bridge, Martin McDonagh, Andrew Scott, and they’re all in this little group talking to each other.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that even though it’s November, people still can’t stop talking about the wedding of the year, Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce. The power couple officially tied the knot during the Fourth of July weekend at Madison Square Garden, and there was plenty of talk both before and after the nuptials. It seemed like everyone who was anyone attended. However, the event has made it incredibly awkward for Conan O’Brien.

According to recent reports, the comedian and talk show host was among the A-listers who scored an invite to the Tayvis wedding. While official photos have not been shared as of yet, many celebrities have spoken out about the magical ceremony, including O’Brien. He’s hyped up a perfect aspect of the wedding, and of course, there’s plenty more to talk about. While speaking with guest Olivia Colman on his Conan O'Brien Needs a Friend podcast, O’Brien recalled watching a group of celebs all talking to each other at the wedding, and it really seems like a dream:.

In a recent development, so my wife and I are watching Phoebe Waller-Bridge, Martin McDonagh, Andrew Scott, and they’re all in this little group talking to each other. This was a couple of months ago, at a big wedding. That wedding.

In a recent development, of course, Swift and Kelce went all out for the surprisingly intimate wedding, and that includes inviting a range of celebrities who you never thought would even be in the same room. Or even if you did think about it, you’d never imagine you’d see it... let alone hear about it. For O’Brien, no matter how many celebrities he’s interviewed over the years or is friends with, he still couldn’t wrap his mind around who all was at the wedding. And he wanted to place himself inside that group:.

In a recent development, everyone in the world was at this wedding, this Taylor Swift wedding. And I look over with my wife, and we see those three talking to each other in a tight little British nodule, like this little hard shell talking together. And I felt like it was high school again, because the three coolest kids in the room were talking, and I just wanted to be part of the conversation.

Sources indicate that seeing a grouping like that would be pretty incredible, and it sounds like O’Brien and his wife were both in awe. I can’t say I blame them being in that environment. Unfortunately, despite being at the wedding like them and having a pretty tight relationship with likely a lot of people there, O’Brien couldn’t exactly push his way into the trio. While he ultimately didn’t move in on them, he could only imagine what would've happened, especially since he hadn’t yet met one of them. He went on:.

It has been revealed that and my wife and I, we were just sitting there like, ‘Oh, my God, to be able to talk to that grouping of those three...’ And I've never met Phoebe Waller-Bridge. I've said to Andrew Scott that would be — she's on my very, very short list next to you of people I would love to meet. But hasn’t happened, and I was maybe 15 feet away, and I couldn’t do it. I was like, ‘I can’t go over there and risk her having saying, ‘Off with you, scum.’.

That definitely would be super awkward. Imagine going over to them, having never met Phoebe Waller-Bridge and just getting straight-up rejected. I wouldn’t be surprised if he had thought about it almost the entire time he was at the wedding. Of course, there’s no telling what would have actually happened, and Colman even said that Waller-Bridge is “wonderful.” Although being in that setting and surrounded by those kinds of people, I can see where O’Brien’s hesitation would come in.

Hopefully, the Toy Story 5 star gets the chance to meet Waller-Bridge in the near future and tell her this story. If anything, it sounds like he had a good time at the wedding, regardless. Even if he wasn’t able to work up the courage to infiltrate an A-lister group.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crime dramas often attract big stars, and MobLand is no exception.
  • Industry observers note that while families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family.
  • Theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crime dramas often attract big stars, and MobLand is no exception. The Paramount+ series stars Tom Hardy as mob fixer Harry Da Souza, with Pierce Brosnan and Paddy Considine in supporting roles and Helen Mirren having a ball as the thoroughly evil matriarch of the Harrigan crime family.

Industry observers note that while families are complicated in even the best of circumstances, that's especially true of the Family. After you've watched the recently released second season of MobLand, try one of these other indicates mixing crime and family (or Family) drama.

Theo James plays army officer Eddie Horniman (a name mentioned as often as possible), heir to the Horniman estate (there it is again) who, upon the death of his father, is named the Duke of Halstead. He learns that his dad was tied to various criminal enterprises, and that his scouse brother is millions of pounds in debt to a drug dealer. What else is the dapper, military-trained Duke to do but learn to navigate the violent underworld while looking cool? You won't be surprised to learn that this British crime drama comes from creator/writer/producer Guy Ritchie, who also has a hand in MobLand. Stream The Gentlemen on Netflix.

In a recent development, another series from Taylor Sheridan (the Yellowstone guy), this pandemic-era hit stars Jeremy Renner as Mike McLusky, head of a family that’s been keeping the peace, through means fair and foul, in the title's company town for decades. The "business" of the corrupt burg happens to be incarceration, and the McLuskys thrive when business is up, even if Mike has slightly different ideas about how to run things. The show deals broadly with systemic racism and inequality in the prison system, but mostly it's a modern-day western about bringing justice to a corrupt town. It will conclude with a fifth season, streaming in 2027. Stream Mayor of Kingstown on Paramount+.

Recent findings suggest that A consistently compelling combination of smart plotting and lurid sex and violence, Banshee stars Antony Starr as Sheriff Lucas Hood...kinda: He's actually a man recently released from prison who takes over that identity when the new sheriff in the small town of Banshee is killed before anyone really has a chance to get to know him. It's all part of a complicated plan to reunite with his lover Ana (Ivana Miličević), and to get back the $15 million in diamonds he lost when he went to jail—but the town is ruled over by various criminal factions, and being sheriff doesn't guarantee any kind of safety; rather, the opposite. Stream Banshee on HBO Max.

Recent findings suggest that mobLand creator Ronan Bennett previously made this acclaimed series that succeeds by maintaining a narrow scope—in this case, a single London council estate. Dushane (Ashley Walters) and Sully (Kane Robinson) are residents and drug dealers at Summerhouse, maintaining an increasingly precarious grip on the criminal element in the community. Most compellingly, the series maintains an extensive supporting cast of locals both in the drug trade and impacted by it, building a disturbingly compelling world. A little confusingly, the first couple of seasons were renamed Top Boy: Summerhouse when the show moved to Netflix, so you'll want to start there before moving on to plain ol' Top Boy. Stream Top Boy: Summerhouse on Netflix.

Based loosely on a nonfiction work investigating the Mafia-like Camorra in Campania, this show focuses on the head of the Savastano clan, Pietro Savastano (Fortunato Cerlino), and his ambitious lieutenant Ciro Di Marzio (Marco D'Amore). When Pietro is arrested at the series' outset, a civil war erupts between family members and among the factions vying for control. Gone are the suits and poker games of many a mob drama—this is a brutal, street-level take on organized crime that forsakes the typical trappings of the genre. Stream Gomorrah on HBO Max.

I'm here for the Pierce Brosnan of it all, but there's also a very strong vibe match in this series that casts the one-time James Bond actor as the head of a literal crime family, even if this one's set in the American West. Adapting Philipp Meyer's 2013 Pulitzer Prize-nominated novel of the same name, the series follows Eli McCullough, a ruthless cattle baron making moves to get in on the burgeoning oil industry in the Rio Grande Valley of 1915. A parallel narrative sees Eli as a young man, kidnapped and raised among a Nʉmʉnʉʉ family. While his backstory lends the character welcome complexity, in the present, he's as determined to build his empire as he is to prepare his son and grandson to take over when he's gone. Stream The Son on Prime Video.

Tom Hardy playing a tough guy isn't terribly unexpected, but here the setting is London, just after the end of the War of 1812. Hardy plays James Delaney, who returns from Africa after ten years away (he says he'd been taken prisoner, but his story doesn't entirely add up) for the funeral of his father. Dad left nothing but a little hunk of land off of Vancouver, not worth much until the war's conclusion creates newly introduced maritime trade opportunities. Suddenly, the United States, Great Britain, and the East India Manufacturer all have eyes on the real estate, and all are willing to do whatever it takes to acquire it—and the stakes become clear once James realizes that his father's cause of death wasn't natural. Stream Taboo on Peacock and Tubi.

According to recent reports, best not ponder too much on the fact that this one's based on a video game, as its pedigree is only hinted at via the levels of action and violence (certainly compared to some of the other shows on this list). Colm Meaney plays Finn Wallace, the absolutely indispensable leader of London's criminal underworld, a man who's been holding everything together for decades, until his shocking murder at the outset of the series (that's not a spoiler, and we spend more time with him via flashbacks). The completely random killing by someone who had no idea what he was doing begets chaos and open violence. Finn's son Sean (Joe Cole) has been raised to take his father's place, but local, Pakistani, and Albanian gangs all move in to take control from the Finn family in the power vacuum. Stream Gangs of London on AMC+.

Industry observers note that the great Forest Whitaker stars as the real-life Bumpy Johnson, who returned from a prison sentence to find his neighborhood falling apart and in the grip of Italian mobsters. A more than capable crime boss in his own right, Johnson resolves to take on the Genovese crime family, eventually forming a tentative alliance with Malcolm X (Nigél Thatch and, later, Jason Alan Carvell). Johnson is the lesser evil as far as Malcolm and others are concerned, and a complicated figure as both crime lord and family man with aspirations of saving his neighborhood. The show will conclude with a two-hour finale, likely airing in 2027. Stream Godfather of Harlem on Hulu.

According to recent reports, adopted into an Italian organized crime family as a baby, Park Joo-hyung took on the name Vincenzo Cassano, eventually becoming a mafia consigliere. After his adoptive father Don Fabio dies, Fabio’s biological son comes gunning for his brother, whom he now sees as competition. Cassano flees to Seoul, on the hunt for a secret stash of money, and in the process discovers a love interest and a newly introduced adversary in a giant business conglomerate that definitely deserves to be taken down. An incredibly popular K-drama, this one definitely puts a unique spin on the tropes of the mob genre. Stream Vincenzo on Netflix.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lawrence Sullivan, better known to the online world as the 'Florida Joker', is in GTA 6.
  • Grand Theft Auto 6's earliest controversy came from its very first official trailer, when Sullivan alleged one of the teaser's similarly tattooed characters was modeled after him.
  • Rockstar seems to have relented to that last request - the vast GTA 6 credits include none other than one Lawrence Sullivan, listed under the 'Local Population' cast, alongside dozens of other names.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lawrence Sullivan, better known to the online world as the 'Florida Joker', is in GTA 6. After accusing Rockstar Games of using his likeness without consent and then demanding a $10m payout, the two parties have seemingly settled their differences.

Grand Theft Auto 6's earliest controversy came from its very first official trailer, when Sullivan alleged one of the teaser's similarly tattooed characters was modeled after him. The former tattoo model, who first went viral because of a mugshot that shared an uncanny resemblance to Batman's Joker, soon called on Rockstar to pay him $2m. His demand rapidly shot up to $10m, before he dropped all legal threats and politely asked to officially work with the developer.

Rockstar seems to have relented to that last request - the vast GTA 6 credits include none other than one Lawrence Sullivan, listed under the 'Local Population' cast, alongside dozens of other names.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 players wasted no time, and quickly found the suspect first teased way back in that original 2023 trailer. In its quest to parody all parts of modern life under capitalism, GTA 6 lets you doomscroll through a social media app called Snapmatic, which flings an endless number of short-form clips and thirst traps at you. If you're lucky enough, or if you scroll for long enough, you'll find a video of Sullivan's in-game counterpart beating up a fake lookalike. He certainly sounds like Sullivan, too.

Sources indicate that "Two years y'all been talking crazy about me," he wrote under a recent Instagram post. "Who got the last laugh now?!".

The GTA 6 credits were illuminating for other reasons, too. We finally know who voices the game's loveable duo, Jason and Lucia, for one. All 34 of the infamously fired Rockstar workers also appear in GTA 6's credits. The controversial move eventually led to accusations of union busting on Rockstar's part, which is presently being investigated as part of an employment tribunal in Scotland.

In a recent development, there can be such a wonderful charm that comes from fan games because the people that make them really are just in it for the love of the (literal) game. They ain't gonna make any money from this thing! So I'm quite tickled by OpenZ, a 3D remake of the 1996 RTS game Z from The Bitmap Brothers that's completely open source (and, thankfully, hand made).

At the moment there's only two levels, though it's sounding like it's the full run of them, described as having been "meticulously restored and polished to an extreme level of detail," with some added improvements thanks to "30 years of RTS game design experience." There's a few new bits to find in this remake too, like new mech and electrobot units.

It sounds like there are bigger intends for the remake overall, presumably for the full game too: "This is only the beginning. Together as a community we can bring Z back to its former glory: more restored classic levels, completely original fresh levels, new units and maybe even multiplayer." As mentioned, it's completely free to download and play too, so where's the harm in giving it a go!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that world of Warcraft: Forever's absolutely had me enthralled, as per my review (and about 220+ hours of my actual life), but that's not to say there aren't problems. Over the weekend and going on into this week, Blizzard's had to play whack-a-mole with both exploits and what appears to be a long-standing bug affecting one of the tanking classes' core mechanics.

It has been revealed that first, those exploits—players discovered that lockboxes contained a sort of quantum loot, in that the actual roll of the lockboxes seemed tied to the player peeking inside of them, rather than what was inside regardless. If you turned off auto-loot, you can open a lockbox without actually pulling the loot into your bag. Then, if you sent that lockbox to another player via mail, they'd get something different.

Essentially, players could simply play a game of mass pass-the-parcel to ensure favorable lockbox results, further busting up the economy after the Blackmaw Hold drama earlier this month. That's since been hotfixed, simply disabling the mechanic, with a more elegant solution to come further down the road: "Today, we’re working on a proper fix that restores the ability to peek and partially loot lockboxes, and makes them otherwise work as intended.".

It has been revealed that meanwhile, the Obsidian Sentinel in Uldaman was briefly rendered lootless. As spotted by WoWHead, players could hop into the dungeon and repeatedly rinse the boss to grab a cheeky 18 or so gold in 15 minutes by vendoring the loot as a max-level character.

While that's not really game-breaking (instance lockouts are limited to five per hour), if you had an organised group of level 60s all funnelling gold to the same guy—like, say, if you were a streamer with a dedicated fanbase that didn't mind wasting a quarter of an hour, or if you were a large-scale RMT operation—there's a bigger problem.

That lootless state turned out to be a band-aid, as Blizzard simply lowered the vendor costs later.

Industry observers note that perhaps the biggest hiccup over the past weekend, though, is the fact that Sunder Armor (and other armor-reducing effects like faerie fire) very well might just not do anything. I hopped in-game to test it on my warrior and saw no noticeable difference between Sunder Armor in both dungeons and the overworld while fighting lower level targets, though my testing capabilities were limited solo, since armor is affected by the level of whoever's attacking the target: And if I rock up to an on-level elite in a dungeon at 60, I tend to die before I can get a good sample.

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

In a recent development, fortunately, I don't need to be too thorough. There's a lot more comprehensive math and log-testing on this github post: "Once an armor debuff goes on, players' and pets' hits barely move, same as the report states. About 5% of the armor drop actually shows up in the damage, and more stacks don't help." The evidence is all pretty convincing.

Recent findings suggest that while those other exploits are annoying oopsies, arguably just a result of players—who find edge cases like water finds cracks—stress-testing the system? The Sunder Armor bug is sort of huge, since that's one of the protection warrior's main group utilities (aside from being a tanky meatshield). It still appears to be filling its primary role of threat generation, but: Yikes.

There's no mention of it in the hotfixes, but I'll enhancement this article if one pops up in the coming days.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that there was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.

Industry observers note that there was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped. Despite the sometimes agonising wait filled with countless spin-offs and collaborations with live service games, we've only seen a vague teaser trailer for the next proper Persona.

P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again. "Persona 6 is not the end," he said in a Sega Samania interview translated by GamesRadar. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day.".

Wada doesn't go into any more detail about how Atlus plans to release Persona games quicker. Is the next mainline game already in development alongside Persona 6, or is Atlus just streamlining how it makes games? Either way, the studio seems to have abandoned its divisive habit of returning to and improving its games after a few years - P3 Portable, P4 Golden, P5 Royal. I imagine that'll cut down on wait times, at least somewhat.

"Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he added. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries.".

In a recent development, as for Persona 6 itself, Wada unsurprisingly "can't say much" about the much-hyped, high-schooling, demon-punching game. "But we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying.".

We don't know much about Atlus' occult sequel, officially, but a massive information leak earlier in the year revealed a full achievement list for Persona 6 and a bunch of other unreleased games, including Kingdom Hearts 4 and an unannounced Sea of Thieves project. Be wary of online spoilers, then.

What is it that warriors fight for?

It has been revealed that each warrior of the Warring States period had their own reasons for riding into battle—be it territory, social standing, the sake of humanity, or their own ambition. This title focuses on those reasons, with battles between evenly matched warriors and an exploration of the bonds between ally and enemy.

Enjoy a full revival of the city development portion of domestic affairs for the first time in nearly 20 years. Freely develop your own castle town, depicted in beautifully evolved graphics.

It has been revealed that experience story mode for the first time in series history. Both series fans and newcomers to the Warring States and historical simulation games can enjoy this story focused on the life of Oda Nobunaga.

Industry observers note that there are many different kinds of smarts, and the kind of smarts I am are absolutely zero help when it comes to games like Astario, a spaceship and space station building factory sim reminiscent of Factorio that just released into early access. I think there's just so many moving parts in ways I can't wrap my head around, but I'm fairly confident that some of you will be, so I'll try to use the smarts I do have to tell you about it a bit more.

Astario puts you in a spaceship in, uh, space, and oh what a substantial space it is. I have no idea if it's a to scale universe or anything, but it certainly looks quite expansive. There is a Minecraftian quality to it in that you must fly about and find resources from things like asteroids and other bits of technological scrap, all of which is divided up into blocks. You can get quite granular with it, inspecting each individual cube up close to see if it's a material that you can make use of, adding it to your haul for use elsewhere.

As you acquire different kinds of blocks, be they functional or structural, you can build up various newly introduced vehicles and "create an imposing machine where all components work together to achieve your goal. Blueprint or design your build out of armor blocks, power supplies, life support components, tools, and production machinery. Construct an orbital station with a stash of cargo containers, or anchor your production base to an asteroid and turn its ores into more blocks, fully automatically. Equip your ship with docking ports for refueling or recharging." How you build things is up to you, you've seemingly got a lot of free reign in terms of artistic expression.

And then of course there's bits of production machinery you can produce that in turn net you recipes and the like so you can continue to improve your ship or space stations. "All production blocks have input and output ports that can be automated using logistic pipes which use request-based item routing," explains the game's Steam page of how techy you can get with it. "Simply hook up your inputs to a cargo container, and the machine will pull what it needs. Mining can be temporarily automated using specialized drills, which mine until the resources within its scope are depleted." If any of this sounds like it's up your alley, then you can pick up Astario on Steam in early access now.

Recent findings suggest that if you're having trouble accessing certain Apple products and services today, you are not alone. As of early Tuesday afternoon, Downdetector demonstrates user reports of problems across multiple Apple services. While Apple's System Status page initially highlighted far fewer issues than Downdetector users reported, the site has since updated to reflect general outages.

According to Apple, the disruptions aren't quite as widespread: Apple says that the App Store, Apple Music, AppleCare on Devices, and Schoolwork are all experiencing outages. Apple says that the App Store and Apple Music "may be slow or unavailable," while AppleCare purchase is currently unavailable. The organization's System Status page reveals an "glitch" with iCloud Account & Sign In. Apple also says there was an outage with the Volume Purchase Program, but that has since been resolved.

It's not clear what's causing the issues with the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud Account & Sign In, or other Apple services at this time. However, the timing is odd. It comes after a number of banks experienced outages on Monday, as well as Microsoft's massive outage the previous week. In addition to all of these outages, the FAA unexpectedly grounded all U.S. flights on Friday, for only the third time in the agency's history.

Team Cherry has declared a livestream that is set to feature an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong's Sea of Sorrow DLC.

GTA 6 may have released last week, but Team Cherry has returned to remind you that Rockstar Games isn't the only developer to have released a long-awaited title after a development cycle that became a meme.

It's still wild to think about, but the DLC-turned-full-sequel has been out for over 12 months after years of silkposting, and thankfully it looks like its DLC – which was announced shortly after launch with a 2026 release date, before striking fear into the hearts of many when that date vanished – won't take quite as long to arrive, as Team Cherry is set to give us an update on it this week.

It has been revealed that join us in 48 hours for Cherry Time! Get ready for a bunch of exciting announcements, plus an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow! Premiering here: youtu.be/M-QUgdcBpZU.

In a post on BlueSky, Team Cherry announced its own Nintendo Direct-equivalent, "Cherry Time!" The stream is set to kick off at 7am PT | 10am ET | 3pm GMT on November 27, 2026, with the post reading "Get ready for a bunch of exciting announcements, plus an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow!".

It's worth noting that Team Cherry said during the initial announcement that we wouldn't know more about the DLC until "shortly before Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow releases," so there's a chance we could be looking at more Hollow Knight Silksong in a matter of days. When the Silksong reveal happened, it was two weeks before the game's release date, so hopefully it'll be no longer than that.

Of course, I do have to flag the terrifying idea that Team Cherry will announce that Sea of Sorrow will be turned into a full game….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if the first season of The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County was any indication, there is no shortage of drama where those women, Mormon or not, are concerned. I’m thrilled to learn that the Hulu series that debuted on the 2026 TV schedule has been renewed for 20 episodes, which likely means we’re guaranteed even more than just Season 2. Although there is one substantial change that I want to see as the series moves forward.

In a recent development, yes, the OC spinoff has its own cast of women connected to the Mormon religion, this time living in Southern California instead of Utah. I am sure there are plenty of stories still to be explored with them as individuals, as well as with the tension in their relationships and friendships. However, with Jen Affleck doing double duty on the OG and OC Mormon Wives reality indicates (which are streaming with a Hulu subscription), and McCall DePron being the older sister of Mayci Neeley, we absolutely need to see more of the women who started this franchise making appearances on the fresh series.

Sources indicate that the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives original series has had a seemingly endless amount of drama and scandals, but things crossed a line into serious domestic and custody disputes in a shortened Season 5 of only five episodes that made it all less fun to watch. While the decision to include women who are not Mormon in the Orange County series is a bit strange, having more appearances from the OG cast would help resolve that problem.

Industry observers note that after the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette, custody issues with her children, and chaos surrounding production of the original series, I will say upfront that we don’t need to see Taylor Frankie Paul head over to the OC with her brand of drama. But after Mayci apologized for crossing the line in defense of her sister McCall, I’d be down to see her and Mikayla Matthews, as well as Layla Taylor, Jessi Ngatikaura, and even Miranda McWhorter show up in sunny Southern California. I feel like not only could any or all of those women bring some fun to the spinoff, but they could also inject some more Mormon energy into the mix.

Recent findings suggest that because Mormon Wives OC’s first season had to introduce us to a lot of newly introduced women, there wasn’t much time in its eight episodes to let us see much of their home lives, families, and relationships. Since it was also introducing many of those women to each other, some of the tension and confrontations felt more manufactured and forced.

Recent findings suggest that now that they’re going into Season 2 with more familiarity, hopefully interactions will start to feel more organic. On top of that, if you bring more original cast members to Orange County, they could provide unique perspectives on their own Mormon lifestyle in Utah while also creating fresh conflicts and storylines for fans of both demonstrates to get excited about and debate.

Recent findings suggest that in other news, fellow Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt is getting her own reality show, so we likely won’t see her back in the Mormon Wives world, at least anytime soon (never say never, right?). But with 20 latest episodes guaranteed with the OC spinoff, I know I’ll be seated and waiting for all the drama to come.
